analyzers.scope: crates/rvc — DutyOrchestrator, keymanager adapters, config, service wiring (~23k LOC)
analyzers.summary: Production code in crates/rvc is smaller and cleaner than the file sizes suggest (roughly half the crate is in-file test modules), with disciplined error handling and almost no unwraps on production paths. The real problems are structural: an optional-wiring pattern that leaves the runtime key-import path disconnected from the orchestrator in production, a whole sibling crate (sync-service) reimplemented inside the orchestrator while the original sits dead, a test-only ServiceBuilder::build_all composition root that diverges from bin/rvc's hand-wiring, and severe config sprawl (60+ flat fields mirrored in CliOverrides with a 275-line manual merge). Several large files mix 1k+ lines of production code with 2-5k-line test modules and 7+ hand-rolled 24-method BeaconNodeClient mocks.

analyzers.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)
analyzers.summary: The two binaries are functionally solid and security-hardened, but bin/rvc/src/main.rs (2712 lines) has become the de facto home of the entire bootstrap: a ~900-line run_validator god-function, a 90-flag clap variant plumbed through five hand-maintained sites into the rvc crate's 65-field CliOverrides, and a dead parallel ServiceBuilder::build_all in the library that has already drifted from production behavior. Duplication is the second theme: the voluntary-exit and prepare-exit commands are ~110-line clones, network preset constants are maintained independently in both binaries' dependency trees, and rvc-keygen copy-pastes its 0o600 file-write block four times with divergent overwrite semantics. Test organization needs attention — ~3.2k lines of bin/rvc/tests exercise library crates they cannot reach main.rs from, while the actual startup path has no automated coverage. rvc-keygen is otherwise well-factored and small; most leverage is in pushing bin/rvc's bootstrap into crates/rvc and collapsing the config plumbing.

analyzers.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)
analyzers.summary: The crate is security-conscious, heavily documented, and well-tested, but it has outgrown its binary-crate shape. It already has a lib target (rvc_signer_bin), yet the entire ~460-line composition root still lives in main.rs outside the lib — forcing tests to shell out to `cargo build` to exercise startup. The type→domain→signing-root policy is implemented three times (gRPC service, HTTP dispatcher, DVT peer service) with verbatim copy-pasted validation helpers and one real behavioral divergence (builder-registration fork version). The gRPC sign metrics are registered but never recorded (dead since the v2 migration), a documented CLI option (--password-dir) cannot work as described, and several source files are 60-82% test code. Extracting the server into a proper library crate plus a shared signing-plan module would remove most of the duplication and make the composition root testable.

analyzers.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)
analyzers.summary: Both crates are functionally solid with strong test discipline (KATs, proptests, redaction conformance), but they carry heavy structural debt from successive security-fix layers accreting side-by-side instead of being consolidated. The dominant problems are duplication at every level: two complete safe-signing stacks in crates/signer (SignerService vs SigningGate) whose safety features (sign timeout, audit-scoped DB, metrics, lock re-check) have diverged; three-plus live copies of the per-duty domain/signing-root derivation plus a four-way duplicated EIP-7044 cap; and a legacy free-function signing API that is production-dead. Meanwhile the crypto crate has become the workspace's de-facto commons — ~20 crates import it just for logging helpers — eroding the documented layering, and crates/signer/src/lib.rs is a 3,008-line god-file. Consolidating the signing core, extracting a logging foundation crate, and deleting the dead API surface would shrink the two crates substantially while making the remaining single implementations easier to keep correct.

The crate is defensively engineered and unusually well documented (fail-closed preflight, WAL pragmas, RAII staged transactions, GVR pinning), but it is carrying its own history: three generations of check/record APIs coexist, only the newest (stage_*) is used in production, and the EIP-3076 rule logic duplicated across them has already drifted — the watermark-equality fix from commit 40b6c1e landed in the two dead paths but not in the production stage path, which the conformance and property suites do not exercise. Structurally, db.rs is a 5,466-line god-file (61% inline tests) with migrations split inconsistently against migration.rs, and a fully-built watermark/prune subsystem has no production caller while its queries run on every sign. The highest-leverage refactor is extracting a single shared rule-evaluation core, deleting the dead API generations, and re-aiming the conformance suite at the path that actually ships.

analyzers.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)
analyzers.summary: The layering itself is sound — beacon does HTTP, bn-manager owns selection/failover/health policy behind the BeaconNodeClient trait, propagator is a thin submission wrapper — and the health/sync/tier logic is clean and well tested. The main maintainability costs are mechanical duplication that compounds per endpoint: four copy-pasted retry loops in the beacon client, a 26-method god-trait that forces ~11 hand-rolled mocks plus a 165-line passthrough impl, and five repeated broadcast-vs-failover dispatch blocks, so adding one endpoint currently touches five or more sites. Secondary issues are files dominated by inline wiremock tests (client.rs is 75% tests, manager.rs 62%), dead configuration (selection_strategy is silently ignored), stringly-typed API structs that duplicate eth-types and push parsing into the orchestrator, and fallback semantics (retry vs failover) configured inconsistently across construction sites including a proposer path that bypasses failover entirely.

These five crates are functionally solid and unusually well-commented (security-review provenance is documented inline), with good trait-based seams and fail-closed defaults; signer-registry and the small validator-store modules are exemplary. The structural debt concentrates in three places: keymanager-api's handlers.rs is a 4181-line monolith whose inline 3200-line integration-test suite and inlined doppelganger concurrency state machine belong in dedicated modules; grpc-signer's client repeats an identical ~55-line RPC pipeline ten times; and secret-provider maintains two divergent copies of the key-loading pipeline where the refresh path silently lacks the metrics, spans, and the boot path lacks the fetch timeout. Cross-cutting, pubkey-hex parsing is re-implemented at least six times despite a canonical helper in eth-types, and several keymanager-api trait contracts are stringly-typed, forcing per-call-site error sanitization.

analyzers.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root
analyzers.summary: eth-types is in good functional health: heavily tested (KAT-anchored against remerkleable, proptest fuzzing), well-documented, and dependency-clean. Its main structural debt is accumulation from incremental security remediations (SEC-6, ISSUE-4.3, ADR-003): a second, parallel SSZ type universe in block_body.rs that duplicates seven root-level types under identical names, four coexisting fork representations with no single conversion point, ~250 lines of copy-pasted hand-written TreeHash boilerplate, and a dead insecure-gate module superseded by a diverged sibling in crates/crypto. None of these are bugs today, but each one raises the cost and risk of the next fork rollout (Fulu/Gloas), which is exactly what this crate exists to absorb.

analyzers.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing
analyzers.summary: These six crates are individually small, thiserror-consistent, and heavily tested, but the workspace carries significant structural debt at the seam with the rvc orchestrator: sync-service's core SyncService is a production-dead twin of logic reimplemented in the orchestrator, doppelganger ships two parallel detection implementations with three copies of the same monotonic-clock formula, and timing's AttestationTimer/run_slot_loop is entirely unused. Test organization is the other recurring problem: block-service/src/service.rs is 3,567 lines of which ~3,000 are one inline test module, and the fat 11-method ValidatorSigner trait forces 100+ line mock stubs in every consumer. A shared convention of narrow per-duty traits (which block-service already demonstrates) plus deleting the dead twins would materially shrink and clarify this layer.

analyzers.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)
analyzers.summary: The workspace is in good structural health: workspace-level dependency management is disciplined, error handling is consistently thiserror-in-libs/anyhow-in-bins (one exception), the architecture-tests CI gate is a genuine strength, and production panic-surface is low (210 unwrap/expect total, mostly justified "slice is exactly N bytes" / metric-registration expects; only 2 panic!-family calls outside tests). The main workspace-level debts are: a 51-method god-trait (BeaconNodeClient) that forces 16 hand-rolled mock implementations, the crypto crate doubling as the workspace logging registry (dragging BLS/keystore code into the HTTP layer), a mirrored-by-comment Web3Signer wire protocol duplicated between client and server, and consensus-critical network constants duplicated in two incompatible formats. ARCHITECTURE.md's dependency graph has drifted materially from the real Cargo graph.

analyzers.scope: Prior review/audit corpus for rvc workspace (REVIEW.md, CODE_REVIEW_REPORT.md, AUDIT-2026-05-30.md, AUDIT-2026-07-18-known-issues.md, test-audit-report.md, .claude/rvc-review-*.md, docs/issues/, plan/security-2026-07-18/)
analyzers.summary: Five substantial reviews (2026-03 through 2026-07) converge on a consistent picture: architecture and slashing-protection core are strong, but the codebase carries recurring structural debt — hand-rolled SSZ/tree-hash with an opaque Vec<u8> block body (root cause of the worst correctness bugs), safety mechanisms that exist but are never wired into production paths, a Keymanager bookkeeping layer disconnected from the real signing registry, ~3,450 unwrap/expect calls in production code, and a test suite whose mocks and self-consistency assertions repeatedly baked in wrong spec assumptions. Two remediation plans (security-2026-07-18 and test-audit docs/issues) already exist and partially overlap; recent commits (0fa0a42..a7f8cdf) show several security items are in flight, so a refactoring plan should target the structural items below rather than the tracked security fixes.

findings.title: Runtime key-import wiring to the orchestrator is optional and never connected in production
findings.detail: KeystoreManagerAdapter and RemoteKeyManagerAdapter update the shared PubkeyMap and fire key_gen_tx only when `with_pubkey_map(...)` was called (`if let Some(ref map) = self.pubkey_map` at keymanager_adapters.rs:399-404, 842-848). rg shows `with_pubkey_map` on these adapters has zero callers outside the defining file: main.rs builds them with only `new(...).with_denylist(...)` (main.rs:1627, 1680). Separately, the orchestrator's `new` and `new_with_attesting_enabled` constructors fabricate a watch channel and immediately drop the sender (`let (_key_gen_tx, key_gen_rx) = watch::channel(0u64)` at coordinator.rs:150/184); `new_with_key_gen`, the only constructor accepting a real receiver, also has zero production callers. Result: `key_gen_rx.has_changed().unwrap_or(false)` at coordinator.rs:322 is always false, so the 'Key set changed, clearing duty cache' path is unreachable, and keys imported via the Keymanager API are added to CompositeSigner but never to the orchestrator's pubkey_map — duty matching for imported keys only works after a restart.
findings.recommendation: Make the pubkey_map + key_gen_tx pair required constructor parameters of both adapters (delete the optional builder methods), and collapse the three stacked DutyOrchestrator constructors (10-13 args each, all #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]) into a single constructor taking an OrchestratorDeps struct that includes the key_gen receiver. This turns the current silent misconfiguration into a compile error and fixes the dormant import path.

findings.title: sync-service crate is dead code; orchestrator reimplements it inline
findings.detail: crates/sync-service ships a fully implemented and tested SyncService (produce_sync_messages, produce_contributions, SyncSigner/SyncBeaconClient traits, 986-line lib + 415-line integration test), but the only symbols the workspace imports from it are the free function `is_sync_committee_aggregator` and `SyncServiceError`. The orchestrator's SyncCommitteeService (sync_committee.rs, 1080 lines) reimplements the same message + contribution pipeline directly against SignerService/BeaconNodeClient, and duplicates the SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE=512 / SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT=4 constants (sync_committee.rs:20-23 vs the same constants in sync-service). OrchestratorError::SyncService (error.rs:44) is never constructed anywhere. ARCHITECTURE.md still documents SyncService as the production path, which is false.
findings.recommendation: Pick one implementation. Either adapt SyncCommitteeService to delegate to sync_service::SyncService (thin adapters for SyncSigner/SyncBeaconClient, keeping the D-3 validator_store gate and SlotContext head_root in the orchestrator layer), or delete the sync-service crate and move is_sync_committee_aggregator into the orchestrator/signer. Remove the dead OrchestratorError::SyncService variant and fix ARCHITECTURE.md either way.

findings.title: ServiceBuilder::build_all / BuiltServices / build_doppelganger_service are test-only scaffolding diverging from real wiring
findings.detail: rg shows build_all has zero callers outside builder.rs itself. It returns an unusual (BuiltServices, FnOnce(BuiltServices) -> (DutyOrchestrator, Handle)) tuple, wires the single-BN BeaconClient (not BnManager), hard-codes epoch=1 for the doppelganger enablement, and constructs build_doppelganger_service, which its own doc comment calls 'legacy one-shot ... (tests / non-production)'. Meanwhile bin/rvc's run_validator (main.rs:1055-~2100, 1000+ lines) hand-wires the same services from the individual build_* methods in a different order, with BnManager, the forward-window machine, liveness loop, keymanager server, etc. Two composition roots exist; only one is real, and the fake one is what the builder's public API advertises (BuiltServices is re-exported from config/mod.rs).
findings.recommendation: Delete build_all, the orchestrator_factory closure, BuiltServices, and build_doppelganger_service (moving the handful of unit tests that use them onto the individual build_* methods) — or, better long-term, invert it: extract the production wiring from run_validator into ServiceBuilder so the composition logic lives once in crates/rvc and main.rs shrinks to CLI/signal handling.

findings.title: Config sprawl: 60+ flat fields mirrored in CliOverrides with a 275-line hand-written merge
findings.detail: Config (types.rs:22-231) is a flat struct of ~65 fields spanning eight unrelated concerns (logfile rotation, tracing, keymanager, grpc-signer TLS, proposer-config URL, monitoring push, circuit breaker, registration batching...). CliOverrides (types.rs:946-1016) duplicates every field as Option<T>, and merge_with_cli (types.rs:651-925) is 275 lines of `if let Some(x) = cli.x { self.x = x.clone() }` repetition. Adding one option currently touches five places: Config field, Default impl (types.rs:338-406), a default_* fn, CliOverrides, and merge_with_cli — plus the clap struct in bin/rvc. Only secret_provider demonstrates the nested-struct pattern that the rest of the file ignores.
findings.recommendation: Group related fields into nested sub-structs (LogfileConfig, TracingConfig, KeymanagerConfig, GrpcSignerConfig, ProposerConfigSource, MonitoringConfig, BuilderLimits) following the existing SecretProviderConfig precedent, and generate the override/merge boilerplate with a small macro_rules (field list written once) or a layered-config approach so merge_with_cli cannot silently miss a field.

findings.title: coordinator.rs: 285-line run() loop with four duplicated shutdown-select blocks, and a ~5,000-line test module in the same file
findings.detail: run() (coordinator.rs:299-585) inlines epoch-boundary work, three phase blocks, deadline math (the bps-in-milliseconds computation appears twice, lines 419-433 and 478-485), the builder-registration select, and four near-identical `tokio::select! { sleep / shutdown_rx.changed() }` blocks each followed by check_shutdown(). The epoch-boundary summary (lines 352-365) loops 32 slots twice just to count duties. Meanwhile the file is 5,711 lines total: production ends at line 742 and a single flat #[cfg(test)] module spans lines 744-5711, mixing timeout tests, fork-transition tests, tracing-span tests, slashing integration, circuit-breaker tests, and sync-gating tests, each with their own mock scaffolding. Navigating or reviewing either half is painful, and the struct carries a blanket #[allow(dead_code)] (line 98) that hides genuinely unused fields.
findings.recommendation: Extract a `wait_for(duration) -> Continue|Shutdown` helper and a `phase_deadline(bps)` helper to deduplicate the four select blocks and the two deadline computations; pull the epoch-boundary block into DutyManagementService. Split the test module into src/orchestrator/coordinator/tests/{timeouts,fork_transition,tracing,slashing,circuit_breaker,sync_gating}.rs (or crate-level tests/), and replace the struct-level #[allow(dead_code)] with per-field annotations or field removal.

findings.title: keymanager_adapters.rs packs 8 unrelated adapters plus free functions into one 3,028-line file
findings.detail: One file contains KeystoreManagerAdapter (with nontrivial file-deletion, denylist, and import-meta sidecar logic), SlashingProtectionAdapter, ValidatorManagerAdapter, DoppelgangerMonitorAdapter, ForwardWindowMonitor, RemoteKeyManagerAdapter, ValidatorConfigManagerAdapter, VoluntaryExitManagerAdapter, plus scan_and_rearm_gate and wall_clock_epoch — followed by ~1,950 lines of tests. KeystoreManagerAdapter and RemoteKeyManagerAdapter duplicate identical `with_pubkey_map` + `notify_key_change` members (lines 73-93 vs 775-789). The crate has 58 occurrences of `format!("0x{}", hex::encode(...))` for pubkey display/keying, several inside this file, despite crypto::pubkey::CanonicalPubkey existing as the declared single source of truth (referenced at orchestrator/utils.rs:110-118).
findings.recommendation: Convert to a keymanager_adapters/ module directory with one file per adapter (keystore.rs, remote_keys.rs, slashing.rs, validator.rs, doppelganger.rs, voluntary_exit.rs, config.rs) and colocated tests. Extract a shared `KeyChangeNotifier { pubkey_map, key_gen_tx }` used by both key adapters, and a `pubkey_hex(pk) -> String` helper (or push CanonicalPubkey/Display use) to eliminate the 0x-format repetition.

findings.title: Seven+ hand-rolled 24-method BeaconNodeClient mocks duplicated across test modules
findings.detail: Each of these sites (plus more in bin/rvc/tests and crates/builder) implements the full BeaconNodeClient trait — ~24 async methods — with `Err(BeaconError::HttpError("mock"))` stubs and one or two real methods (rg counts 19-47 'mock' stub lines per file). sync_committee.rs and slot_context.rs each contain two separate such impls. Any new method on BeaconNodeClient forces edits to every one of these mocks, which is exactly the kind of friction that discourages extending the trait.
findings.recommendation: Add a `test-utils` feature to bn-manager exporting a single ErroringBeacon base mock (all methods default to Err) with overridable closures or a builder for the few methods a test cares about — or derive mocks with mockall. Then delete the per-file impl blocks; expected reduction is well over 1,000 lines.

findings.title: AggregationService::maybe_produce_aggregations is a 415-line function with mirrored Electra/pre-Electra branches
findings.detail: The single function spans lines 46-459. Inside the per-duty loop, the Electra branch (lines 246-305) and pre-Electra branch (lines 306-365) are structurally identical (build AggregateAndProof, try_tree_hash_root guard, sign, push) differing only in types and log strings; the two submit blocks (lines 368-410 and 412-458) are likewise ~45-line clones differing only in the VersionedSignedAggregateAndProof wrapper. The `timeout → warn → RVC_AGGREGATIONS_TOTAL[FAILED].inc() → continue` idiom repeats 8 times here, and the same match-on-timeout logging pattern appears 5 more times in duty_management.rs (fetch_epoch_duties lines 65-117, check_reorg lines 208-274).
findings.recommendation: Split into produce_one_aggregate(duty) -> Option<Aggregate> and a generic sign_and_wrap helper parameterized over the proof type (both share TreeHash + signing shape), plus a submit_versioned(versioned, label) helper. Add a crate-local `timed(op_name, timeout, fut)` combinator that logs and increments the failure metric uniformly, and reuse it in duty_management.rs.

findings.title: Stringly-typed config enums validated in multiple divergent places
findings.detail: slashed_validators_action is a String whose valid values are listed twice: Config::validate (types.rs:547-555) and SlashedAction::FromStr (slashing_monitor.rs:16-30) — main.rs then re-parses the already-validated string. broadcast: Vec<String> is validated at types.rs:515-530 and the same literals are re-matched in effective_broadcast_topics (types.rs:620-638). tracing_exporter and BeaconNodeEntry.roles are also free-form strings. Each pair of lists can drift independently, and typos are only caught at runtime validation rather than deserialization.
findings.recommendation: Make SlashedAction, BroadcastTopic, TracingExporter, and BnRole serde-deserializable enums (kebab-case rename) used directly as Config field types, deleting the duplicate match arms in validate() and effective_broadcast_topics(); Config::validate keeps only cross-field rules (e.g. 'none' exclusivity).

findings.title: PubkeyMap is stringly-keyed, causing per-slot re-normalization, linear scans, and an O(validators×64×duties) index lookup
findings.detail: PubkeyMap = Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, PublicKey>>> keyed by hex strings. All production insertion sites already produce canonical 0x-lowercase keys (build_pubkey_map at config/builder.rs:500-508; keymanager adapters), yet find_pubkey (utils.rs:79-108) keeps a case-insensitive O(n) linear fallback, get_duties_for_slot (utils.rs:198-227) clones the entire map and re-normalizes every key on every call (invoked twice per slot: attestation + aggregation), and submit_committee_subscriptions does a per-duty linear `.find` with normalize on both sides (duty_management.rs:357-359). Worst, prepare_proposers resolves each validator's index by scanning 64 slots × all duties per validator per epoch (duty_management.rs:287-312), even though a pubkey→index map already exists and is maintained by the liveness loop (IndexToPubkeyHex, liveness_loop.rs:46) and by main.rs's validator_index_map.
findings.recommendation: Re-key PubkeyMap by [u8; 48] (or a CanonicalPubkey newtype) and normalize duty pubkeys once at DutyTracker ingestion; delete find_pubkey's linear fallback. Share one pubkey→validator_index registry (promote the liveness loop's IndexToPubkeyHex into a small shared component) and use it in prepare_proposers instead of the nested duty-cache scan.
findings.scope: crates/rvc — DutyOrchestrator, keymanager adapters, config, service wiring (~23k LOC)

findings.title: process_attestation_duty: 330-line function built from 12 early-return AttestationResult constructions
findings.detail: attestation.rs:224-554 repeats `return AttestationResult { validator_index, slot, success: false, error: Some(...) }` twelve times, each hand-copying the same three fields; the happy-path logic is buried between them. The versioned-attestation construction (lines 466-510) also duplicates the index-zeroing clone for Fulu and Electra branches that differ only in the enum constructor.
findings.recommendation: Refactor the body into an inner `async fn attest(...) -> Result<(), String>` using `?`, and build the AttestationResult once at the call site from the Result; collapse the Fulu/Electra arms into one block that selects the constructor after building the shared SingleAttestation.

findings.title: Orchestrator crate accumulates unrelated ops features and a confusing duty_tracker name collision
findings.detail: crates/rvc hosts beaconcha.in monitoring push (monitoring.rs, with its own reqwest client and OS-specific /proc parsing), proposer-config URL refresh (config_url.rs), and voluntary-exit file helpers (prepare_exit.rs, submit_exit.rs) — none of which touch the orchestrator. Meanwhile `crate::duty_tracker` (src/duty_tracker/, 44 lines) is only the gRPC Healthz service, but shares its module name with the external `duty_tracker` crate imported throughout the same crate (`use duty_tracker::DutyTracker` in coordinator.rs vs `crate::duty_tracker::service::DutyTrackerService`), and its proto trait is also named DutyTracker. Small dead code nearby: OrchestratorError::Shutdown, ::InvalidPubkey, and ::BeaconTimeout are constructed only inside error.rs's own tests.

Move prepare_exit/submit_exit next to their only consumers in bin/rvc/src/commands (or an ops-support module), and group monitoring.rs + config_url.rs under a background_tasks module. Delete the three never-constructed OrchestratorError variants.

findings.title: run_validator is a ~900-line god-function while ServiceBuilder::build_all is a dead, drifting parallel bootstrap path
findings.detail: run_validator (bin/rvc/src/main.rs:1055-1953) inlines the entire startup sequence: slashing DB open + integrity + permissions, keystore lock, deletion denylist, beacon/BnManager creation, genesis-root validation, keystore + cloud-provider key loading with two separate Arc::try_unwrap ownership dances (main.rs:1247, 1283), gRPC signer wiring, forward-window/doppelganger setup, secret-refresh task, keymanager API assembly, orchestrator construction, slashing monitor, gRPC/metrics/monitoring/proposer-config tasks, and shutdown. It also parses the genesis validators root twice with duplicated error handling (main.rs:1186-1211). Meanwhile crates/rvc/src/config/builder.rs:703 has ServiceBuilder::build_all which does the same wiring but is called by nothing (rg finds only the definition), and has already drifted from production: it wires the deprecated backward DoppelgangerService (builder.rs:762-766, which main.rs:1355 explicitly says is 'no longer the production mechanism'), uses the denylist-blind build_key_manager (builder.rs:722) instead of build_key_manager_filtered, and hardcodes enablement epoch 1 (builder.rs:745). Two bootstrap paths where one is dead and wrong is worse than one.
findings.recommendation: Delete build_all/BuiltServices or rewrite it to be the single production bootstrap. Extract run_validator into phase functions in crates/rvc (e.g., a bootstrap module next to startup.rs): open_slashing_db(config) -> SlashingDb, load_signing_keys(config, denylist) -> CompositeSigner, wire_signing_enablement(...), spawn_background_tasks(...). main.rs should shrink to CLI parsing, logging init, and a call into the library, which also makes the startup sequence unit-testable (today it is only testable end-to-end).
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: Adding one CLI flag requires touching 5 places: 90-flag Start variant, manual destructure, CliOverrides literal, 65-field CliOverrides struct, 274-line merge_with_cli
findings.detail: The Commands::Start enum variant spans main.rs:43-391 (~90 inline fields), is destructured field-by-field at main.rs:506-582 (76 bindings), and manually copied into a CliOverrides literal at main.rs:628-718 including repetitive bool-to-Option conversions (`if init_slashing_db { Some(true) } else { None }` repeated for 9 flags). CliOverrides itself is a 65-field struct (types.rs:946-1016), and merge_with_cli (types.rs:651-925) is 274 lines of near-identical `if let Some(ref x) = cli.x { self.x = ... }` blocks. Every new flag touches all five sites across two crates; the clap enum variant even needs `#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]` (main.rs:40) to compile clean.
findings.recommendation: Replace the inline Start variant with `Start(StartArgs)` where StartArgs is a `#[derive(clap::Args)]` struct composed of flattened groups (`#[command(flatten)] logging: LoggingArgs`, TracingArgs, KeymanagerArgs, GrpcSignerArgs, ProposerArgs, MonitoringArgs...). Move the clap derive onto CliOverrides itself (or provide `impl From<StartArgs> for CliOverrides`), eliminating the destructure and the hand-written literal. Consider generating merge_with_cli with a small declarative macro over the field list so struct and merge cannot drift.
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: voluntary_exit.rs and prepare_exit.rs are ~110-line near-verbatim clones with a panic-based Arc unwrap
findings.detail: Lines 24-135 of both files are essentially identical: beacon client creation, 0x pubkey normalization, validator-index resolution, current-epoch derivation from genesis time, Config construction, denylist load, key-manager build, slashing DB open, CompositeSigner/SignerService assembly, pubkey parse, fork-schedule fetch, and sign_voluntary_exit. Only the last ~15 lines differ (submit to BN + --confirm gate vs write_exit_to_file). Both also contain `Arc::try_unwrap(key_manager).unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("single reference to key_manager"))` (voluntary_exit.rs:120-121, prepare_exit.rs:103-104) — a panic in a production path, violating the CLAUDE.md error-handling convention, where main.rs handles the same situation with an anyhow error (main.rs:1283-1285). The duplicated test `test_pubkey_prefix_normalization` in both files re-implements the normalization inline instead of testing shared code, so it guards nothing.
findings.recommendation: Extract a shared `build_signed_exit(args) -> anyhow::Result<(SignedVoluntaryExit, u64)>` helper (commands/mod.rs or crates/rvc) covering steps common to both commands; each command becomes ~30 lines of prologue/epilogue. Replace the panicking Arc::try_unwrap with `?` propagation. Extract pubkey normalization into a function and test that.
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: Network presets (genesis roots, fork versions, genesis times) duplicated between rvc-keygen and the rvc config crate
findings.detail: bin/rvc-keygen/src/network.rs:12-54 hardcodes mainnet/hoodi/holesky/sepolia genesis_fork_version, genesis_validators_root (as [u8; 32]), and capella_fork_version. crates/rvc/src/config/network.rs:17-43 hardcodes the same four networks' genesis_time and genesis_validators_root as hex strings. The same mainnet root literal `4b363db94e28...` also appears in crates/rvc/src/config/builder.rs:1063 and crates/rvc/src/startup.rs tests. Both files independently implement case-insensitive name parsing with different error text, and both must be edited (in different byte/hex formats) when a network is added or deprecated — a real risk given holesky/sepolia were recently added to one side.
findings.recommendation: Create a single `NetworkPreset` table in crates/eth-types (already a dependency of both binaries, zero internal deps): name, genesis_fork_version, genesis_validators_root, capella_fork_version, genesis_time. Have keygen's KeygenNetwork and rvc's Network methods delegate to it, and derive FromStr/Display from the one table.
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: bin/rvc/tests tier suites (~3.2k lines) test library crates, not the binary, and include tautological cases
findings.detail: tier2_safety.rs (924 lines), tier3_operations.rs (978), tier4_advanced.rs (940), and integration_test.rs exclusively import and exercise `rvc::config`, `rvc::slashing_monitor`, `rvc::startup`, `bn_manager`, `builder` — all library crates. Since bin/rvc has no lib target, these integration tests cannot touch any code in main.rs; they live one crate away from the code they cover and force the binary to rebuild to run them. Several are tautological, e.g., tier3_operations.rs:52-55 `empty_proposer_nodes_returns_none` constructs a Config with an empty vec and asserts the vec is empty, and `proposer_pool_separate_from_main_pool` (tier3_operations.rs:37-49) asserts two hand-set config fields differ.
findings.recommendation: Move these suites into crates/rvc/tests (and crates/bn-manager/tests) next to the code they exercise, prune the assertion-free/tautological cases, and reserve bin/rvc/tests for genuine CLI-level tests (spawning the binary via assert_cmd/escargot to cover flag parsing, exit codes, and the startup path that currently has zero automated coverage).
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: Keymanager API server assembly is a 125-line inline block with a duplicated gate-rearm branch and a 14-positional-arg constructor
findings.detail: main.rs:1595-1720 inlines token ensure/permission-warn, address parsing, six adapter constructions, doppelganger-monitor selection, and server spawn inside run_validator. The `scan_and_rearm_gate` call is duplicated verbatim in both branches of the monitor selection (main.rs:1658-1664 and 1670-1676). KeymanagerServer::new is then called with 14 positional arguments (main.rs:1696-1711) — mixed Arcs, a String token, an address, two bools, and a Duration — which is unreadable and fragile at the call site (adjacent same-typed params can be swapped without a compile error).
findings.recommendation: Extract the whole block into `rvc::keymanager_adapters::spawn_keymanager_api(config, Deps { composite_signer, slashing_db, validator_store, ... }) -> anyhow::Result<()>` in crates/rvc where the adapters already live. Hoist scan_and_rearm_gate above the branch. Replace the 14-arg constructor with a KeymanagerServerConfig struct or builder in crates/keymanager-api.
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: Proposer-nodes support builds a multi-node BnManager and then discards it, silently using only the first endpoint
findings.detail: main.rs:1526-1539 calls builder.build_proposer_bn_manager() (which constructs a full BnManager with failover/health-scoring over all --proposer-nodes endpoints), but the match at main.rs:1542-1560 binds the result as `Some(_proposer_mgr)` — underscore-ignored — and instead constructs a brand-new single-endpoint BeaconClient from `config.proposer_nodes[0]` with an inline comment admitting the type mismatch ("We need an Arc<BeaconClient> - but proposer_mgr is an Arc<BnManager>"). The comma-delimited CLI flag (main.rs:304-305) advertises a dedicated proposer pool, but nodes 2..n and the built manager's failover are dead; the manager only serves as a Some/None signal.
findings.recommendation: Make BeaconBlockAdapter generic over (or wrap) `Arc<dyn BeaconNodeClient>` so the proposer BnManager is actually used for block production with failover — or, if single-node is the intended semantics, delete build_proposer_bn_manager, accept a single URL, and document it. Either way, remove the discarded construction.
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: Tracing sample-rate uses a float sentinel to detect 'default', making an explicit 0.01 indistinguishable and silently overridable by env
findings.detail: build_tracing_config (main.rs:948-956) decides whether OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG may override the configured rate by checking `(sample_rate - 0.01).abs() < f64::EPSILON` — i.e., 'still at default'. An operator who explicitly passes `--tracing-sample-rate 0.01` gets silently overridden by the env var, and the CLI flag has `default_value_t = 0.01` (main.rs:207-208) so `tracing_sample_rate: Some(...)` is always populated in CliOverrides, defeating the None-means-unset convention every other field uses. This env-precedence logic also lives in the binary while all other config precedence lives in Config::merge_with_cli — two homes for layering rules.
findings.recommendation: Make tracing_sample_rate an Option<f64> end-to-end (drop the clap default_value_t; apply the 0.01 fallback at resolution time), and move the OTEL_* env fallbacks into Config resolution (or the telemetry crate) so precedence is defined in exactly one place. Same treatment for the OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT fallback at main.rs:943-946.
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: rvc-keygen duplicates the 0o600 create_new file-write block four times with divergent non-unix overwrite behavior
findings.detail: The cfg(unix)/cfg(not(unix)) 'create-new file with mode 0o600' pattern is copy-pasted in write_mnemonic_backup (new_mnemonic.rs:19-52), write_with_permissions (new_mnemonic.rs:258-283), bls_to_execution.rs:77-98, and exit.rs:52-73. The copies have already diverged: on non-unix, new_mnemonic keeps `create_new(true)` (refuses to clobber an existing file) while bls_to_execution.rs:94-98 and exit.rs:69-73 fall back to plain `fs::write`, which silently overwrites an existing signed message. Tests in exit.rs:255-269 and bls_to_execution.rs:311-324 then re-duplicate the same block a fifth and sixth time with the comment 'Use the same write logic as run()' — proof the logic is untestably inlined.
findings.recommendation: Add one `fs_util::write_new_0600(path, bytes) -> Result<()>` module in rvc-keygen (or crates/crypto, which both binaries use), with create_new semantics on all platforms, and call it from all four sites; tests then exercise the helper directly.
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: Slashing monitor communicates through a watch::Sender with a dropped receiver, used as a mutable bool
findings.detail: main.rs:1760-1764 creates `let (tx, _rx) = tokio::sync::watch::channel(false)` — receiver immediately dropped — with the comment "We'll re-purpose: the slashing monitor just cancels the shutdown_token". check_slashed_validators (slashing_monitor.rs:32-37) takes `&watch::Sender<bool>` as an out-parameter, the caller then polls `*tx.borrow()` (main.rs:1787) and cancels the CancellationToken itself. A channel type is being used as a shared mutable flag, obscuring the actual contract ("did this check request shutdown?"). The loop also hardcodes `Duration::from_secs(12) * 32` (main.rs:1768-1769) instead of eth_types::SECONDS_PER_SLOT/SLOTS_PER_EPOCH used elsewhere in the same file (main.rs:1640-1641), and the whole loop lives inline in run_validator rather than in the slashing_monitor module.
findings.recommendation: Change check_slashed_validators to return an enum (e.g., SlashedOutcome::{NoAction, ShutdownRequested}); move the epoch-tick loop into `rvc::slashing_monitor::spawn(beacon, store, action, shutdown_token)` using the eth_types timing constants; the caller just spawns it.
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: 615-line #[cfg(test)] module in bin main.rs largely tests the telemetry crate, contains a vacuous test and a duplicated test harness
findings.detail: The test module (main.rs:2097-2712) includes: RUST_LOG parity tests (2672-2711) and init_tracing tests (2325-2350) that call only telemetry:: functions — they belong in crates/telemetry (the comment at 2668 even says they 'mirror the rvc-signer parity tests', i.e., a third copy exists); test_init_logging_none_config_returns_none (2295-2302) which constructs a local None and asserts it is_none — it verifies nothing about production code (its own comment concedes 'verified by code review'); and a SharedBuf MakeWriter test double defined twice verbatim within the same module (2518-2534 and 2608-2624).
findings.recommendation: Move the telemetry-behavior tests into crates/telemetry as the single shared home for both binaries' parity guarantees; delete the vacuous test; define SharedBuf once at test-module scope. Keep in main.rs only tests that exercise binary-local code (clap parsing, build_tracing_config, apply_fork_compatibility_result).
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: new_mnemonic/existing_mnemonic run() take 9-10 positional args (bool/str soup), inconsistent with the Args-struct style of sibling subcommands
findings.detail: new_mnemonic::run (10 params) and generate_from_seed (9 params) both carry #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] and mix adjacent bools and &str values; call sites read as `..., true, &password, false)` (e.g., new_mnemonic.rs:351, existing_mnemonic.rs:83-85) where pbkdf2/dry_run are indistinguishable without counting positions — every one of the ~20 test call sites repeats this. Meanwhile bls_to_execution.rs:15 and exit.rs:13 in the same binary already use dedicated Args structs (BlsToExecutionArgs, ExitArgs), so the crate has two conventions for the same problem.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a GenerateArgs struct (network, output_dir, num_validators, start_index, withdrawal_address, kdf: EncryptionKdf, dry_run) shared by new_mnemonic and existing_mnemonic, matching the existing Args-struct convention; replace the pbkdf2 bool with the EncryptionKdf enum that already exists in crypto.
findings.scope: bin/rvc and bin/rvc-keygen (CLI entry points and bootstrap, ~10.2k LOC)

findings.title: Composition root (run_serve, ~460 lines) lives in main.rs outside the lib target; tests must shell out to cargo build
findings.detail: The crate is nominally split into lib (rvc_signer_bin) + thin main.rs, but main.rs is 1299 lines and `run_serve` (main.rs:359-821) is a single god function doing everything: crypto-provider install, config resolution, password loading, backend construction (with cfg(feature=dvt) tuple gymnastics at 404-462), TLS validation, dry-run printing, hot-reload spawn, metrics server, a ~75-line slashing-DB open/TOCTOU policy (552-611), gate construction, CN allow-list loading, DVT peer-service assembly, HTTP listener spawn, gRPC router assembly, SIGHUP log-reload wiring, and shutdown sequencing. `build_dvt_backend` and `resolve_config` are also main.rs-only. Because none of this is in the lib, integration_polish.rs's `bin_path()` (lines 20-35) runs `cargo build -p rvc-signer-bin` from inside a unit test to get a binary to spawn — a nested build under the test runner that breaks under --locked/offline CI and serializes on the target-dir lock. Error handling throughout is `Box<dyn std::error::Error>` with `format!(...).into()` string errors, contrary to CLAUDE.md's thiserror/anyhow guidance.
findings.recommendation: Move server assembly into the lib: a `server` module with `pub async fn run(resolved: ResolvedConfig, shutdown: CancellationToken) -> Result<(), ServerError>` decomposed into `open_slashing_db()`, `build_backend()`, `build_grpc_router()`, `spawn_http_api()` (each unit-testable), using a thiserror `ServerError`. main.rs shrinks to CLI parse + logging init + `server::run`. Then graduate the lib into `crates/signer-server` so bin/rvc-signer becomes a thin shim, matching the workspace's bin/rvc → crates/rvc pattern. Replace integration_polish's cargo-build-in-test with tests/ files using `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_rvc-signer")` or, better, direct calls to the now-library `server::run`.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: Ten v2 gRPC handlers repeat an identical ~20-line prelude and a 6-line gate-or-fallback dispatch
findings.detail: Every one of the 10 v2 sign handlers in service.rs repeats verbatim: extract_client_cn → authorize_client_cn → into_inner → validate_pubkey → pubkey_hex → Span record → fork_info.ok_or_else → validate_fork_version → validate_gvr (e.g. 494-505, 593-604, 640-651, 803-814 …), and the seven non-slashable handlers additionally repeat the same `if let Some(gate) = &self.gate { gate.sign_X(...).map_err(gate_err_to_status)? } else { sign_via_backend(...) }` block (613-618, 770-777, 832-839, 887-892, 954-961, 1024-1031, 1081-1086) plus a near-identical `tracing::info!` success log. The trait impl is ~630 lines of which perhaps 200 are type-specific.
findings.recommendation: Extract a `RequestCtx` helper: `fn sign_prelude<T>(&self, req: Request<T>) -> Result<(T, RequestCtx), Status>` returning {client_cn, pubkey_bytes, pubkey_hex, current_version, gvr} (with a fork-info-less variant for builder registration), and an `async fn dispatch_non_slashable(&self, ctx, root, method: GateMethod) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Status>` that centralizes the gate-or-backend fallback. Each handler shrinks to decode + domain + root + one dispatch call.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: Validation helpers and decode blocks copy-pasted verbatim between service.rs and dvt/peer_service.rs
findings.detail: `validate_pubkey`, `validate_fork_version`, `validate_gvr`, `ssz_err`, `pubkey_hex` are byte-identical private functions in both service.rs (324-370, 435-437) and dvt/peer_service.rs (104-150). The ~40-line proto-AttestationData→eth_types::AttestationData decode block (source/target/beacon_block_root try_into with per-field error strings) is duplicated (service.rs:656-696 vs peer_service.rs:336-376), as is the block-signing-root sequence decode_beacon_block_ssz → DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER → try_tree_hash_root → compute_signing_root (service.rs:507-516 vs peer_service.rs:236-245). peer_service.rs's module doc also references a "spawn_blocking + Handle::block_on pattern used in service.rs" that no longer exists there (the gate owns it now) — stale doc drift caused by the copy.
findings.recommendation: Add a `grpc_common` (or `proto_convert`) module in the lib with the five validators, `attestation_data_from_proto(proto) -> Result<AttestationData, Status>`, and `beacon_block_signing_root(ssz, fork_id, version, gvr) -> Result<(u64, [u8;32]), Status>`; use it from both services and fix the stale doc comment.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: Type→domain→signing-root policy implemented three times across transports, with one real divergence (builder fork version)
findings.detail: The mapping "message type → domain constant → object to hash → slashing class" exists in three parallel implementations: gRPC service.rs handlers, HTTP dispatch.rs `plan_sign` (the cleanest — it produces a `SignPlan { signing_root, slashing }`), and DVT peer_service.rs. They have already diverged: gRPC `sign_builder_registration` honors a request-supplied `genesis_fork_version` (service.rs:1008-1019, empty ⇒ mainnet), while the HTTP path hardcodes `BUILDER_FORK_VERSION = [0,0,0,0]` (dispatch.rs:45) with a comment admitting non-mainnet handling is a follow-up — identical requests over the two transports produce different signatures on non-mainnet networks. Every new fork/message type must be added in three places.
findings.recommendation: Promote dispatch.rs's SignPlan/Slashing engine into a transport-neutral module (input: typed eth-types message + fork inputs; output: signing root + slashing class) and have both the gRPC handlers and HTTP dispatcher consume it, keeping only proto/serde decode per transport. Resolve the builder-fork-version divergence deliberately (thread the network genesis fork version through both paths) as part of the unification.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: gRPC sign metrics are registered but never recorded; SignerServiceImpl.metrics and classify_error are dead code
findings.detail: `SignerMetrics.sign_total`, `sign_duration_seconds`, and `sign_errors_total` (metrics.rs:20-22) are created and registered but never incremented/observed anywhere in production code — only tests touch them (one scrape test increments manually, routes.rs:1286). The `SignerServiceImpl.metrics` field (service.rs:123) is written by `with_metrics` (210) and never read: the v2 handler migration dropped all per-RPC metric recording on the gRPC path while the HTTP path records `http_sign_total`/`http_sign_duration_seconds` (routes.rs:167-176). `classify_error` (metrics.rs:193) is referenced only by its own unit tests. Operators scraping :9101 see permanently-zero gRPC sign series alongside live HTTP series.
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly: either record sign_total/duration/errors in the v2 handlers (mirroring the HTTP path's type × outcome labeling from Issue 4.5, wiring classify_error back in), or delete the three collectors, the `metrics` field, `with_metrics`, and `classify_error`. Given the HTTP precedent, recording is the better choice; either way remove the dead field.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: --password-dir cannot work as documented: the directory path is read as a single file
findings.detail: The CLI documents `--password-dir` as "Path to the directory containing per-keystore password files" (main.rs:82-83) and it is plumbed through SignerSection/CliOverrides/ResolvedConfig, but the only consumer, `load_serve_password` (main.rs:1031-1043), does `std::fs::read_to_string(dir)` on the directory path — which fails with "Is a directory" on Unix. No per-keystore-password logic exists anywhere (BasicSigner::load takes exactly one password for all keystores). Additionally, when neither source is set the function silently returns an empty-string password (main.rs:1041-1042) despite the comment "prompt or use empty string" — no prompt exists, so a misconfigured deployment proceeds and fails later with confusing per-keystore decrypt errors.
findings.recommendation: Either implement per-keystore password files (read `<pubkey>.txt` from the dir in BasicSigner::load/reload) or delete the `--password-dir` option and its config plumbing. Make the no-password-source case an explicit startup error (or implement the promised prompt) instead of defaulting to an empty password.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: Config plumbing requires touching six places per knob; manual *_is_default detection silently mis-resolves explicit CLI values
findings.detail: Adding one setting touches: ServeArgs (main.rs), SignerSection or HttpSection (config.rs), the CliOverrides mirror struct (config.rs:133-165, 30+ fields), resolve_config's hand-rolled default detection (`has_config && args.listen_address == DEFAULT_LISTEN_ADDRESS`, main.rs:973-996 incl. cfg(dvt) permutations), merge_with_cli, and ResolvedConfig. The string-comparison heuristic has a real edge case: a user who passes `--config file.toml --listen-address 127.0.0.1:50052` (explicitly the default value) has their explicit CLI flag silently overridden by the file. The backend is also stringly typed end-to-end: `Backend` → Display → `ResolvedConfig.backend: String` → `parse_backend()` back to the enum (main.rs:1050-1058) plus raw comparisons like `resolved.backend == "dvt"` (main.rs:479).
findings.recommendation: Make CLI args `Option<T>` (drop clap default_value; keep defaults in one place in merge_with_cli), which eliminates every *_is_default flag and the mirror-struct churn — or use clap's `ArgMatches::value_source` if defaults must stay visible in --help. Move ServeArgs into the lib's config.rs so merge can take `&ServeArgs` directly and CliOverrides can be deleted. Keep `Backend` as an enum through ResolvedConfig.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: Two proto compilations of signer.proto / signer.v2.proto produce incompatible generated types across crates
findings.detail: bin/rvc-signer and crates/grpc-signer each run tonic_build over the same proto/signer.proto and proto/signer.v2.proto, yielding two structurally-identical-but-distinct Rust type sets. rvc-signer-bin's dev-deps pull in grpc-signer for integration tests, so any end-to-end test crossing the client/server boundary deals with two `SignRequest` types. Both build.rs files also keep compiling the deprecated v1 proto solely because grpc-signer's connect path still uses v1 ListPublicKeys (deletion deferred to ISSUE-1.9 per the build.rs comment).
findings.recommendation: Create a small `crates/signer-proto` crate that compiles both protos once (server + client stubs behind features) and re-exports the generated modules; make both bin/rvc-signer and crates/grpc-signer depend on it. Then finish the ISSUE-1.9 migration (v2 ListPublicKeys in GrpcRemoteSigner::connect) and delete signer.proto and the v1 stubs in one place.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: Test code dominates source files (routes.rs 82% tests) and two test-only top-level modules have opaque names
findings.detail: routes.rs is 1881 lines of which 1549 are the in-file tests module (82%); http_api/tls.rs 661/1097, service.rs 615/1737, backend/dvt.rs 492/744, config.rs 463/751. The routes.rs tests are router-level integration tests (tower::oneshot over the full Router with a real gate + in-memory slashing DB), not unit tests of the handlers, so the "tests at the bottom of the file" convention has scaled poorly — the production code is a 330-line island at the top of a 1.9k-line file. Two cfg(test)-only top-level modules have names that convey nothing about coverage: integration_polish.rs (706 lines: CLI/TOML precedence, metrics wiring, hot-reload, and binary-spawning tests) and cross_transport.rs (gate-sharing regression). Integration test filenames in tests/ are keyed to audit-issue IDs (tonic_limits_m10.rs, insecure_flag_h9.rs, dvt_sni_pinning_l1.rs, audit_cn_m4.rs, hot_reload_l6.rs), which will become opaque once the audit context fades.
findings.recommendation: Move the router-level suites out of routes.rs/tls.rs into either http_api submodule test files or tests/ (they already use only pub(crate) test_support + the router); rename integration_polish.rs by behavior (e.g. config_precedence.rs + cli_startup.rs) and relocate the binary-spawning cases to tests/ using CARGO_BIN_EXE. Rename issue-ID test files to behavior names, keeping the issue ID in a doc comment.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: TLS logic is split across two same-named modules with mixed concerns; copy-pasted wrong doc comment
findings.detail: `src/tls/` holds the tonic/gRPC PEM config (TlsConfig) while `src/http_api/tls.rs` (1097 lines) is a grab-bag of five concerns: rustls crypto-provider install (install_crypto_provider, 424), PEM→DER loading (read_certs/read_key, 235-254), ServerConfig/verifier building (168-212), the entire hardened HTTPS accept loop with semaphore/drain/handshake-timeout logic (278-413), and the audit-CN helper `audit_cn` (94-98) — plus 660 lines of tests. The two modules also duplicate the read-file-with-path-in-error pattern differently (TlsError::ReadCert vs HttpTlsError::Read). src/tls/mod.rs:35-39 carries a copy-pasted doc comment: `to_client_tls_config` is documented as "Build a tonic ServerTlsConfig with mTLS enabled. Client certificates are required…" — the server text pasted onto the client builder.
findings.recommendation: Split http_api/tls.rs into tls_config.rs (provider install + PEM loading + ServerConfig build) and accept_loop.rs (serve_https/serve_one), and move `audit_cn` next to audit::cn. Rename src/tls to grpc_tls (or fold both under a `transport` module) so `tls` is not two different things. Fix the to_client_tls_config doc comment.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: Deprecated v1 SignerService kept fully compiled though every method returns Unimplemented
findings.detail: The v1 `SignerService` impl (service.rs:459-478) returns `Status::unimplemented` from all three methods and is not registered on the live listener (SS-1 fix), yet the trait impl, the lib.rs v1 re-exports (SignerServiceServer, SignRequest/SignResponse etc.), ~90 lines of v1 unit tests asserting Unimplemented (service.rs:1252-1289, 1596-1620), and audit/mod.rs's "backward-compat re-exports for the v1 handler" all remain. The stated justification is a hypothetical future off-by-default insecure listener (ADR-010) that is explicitly "NOT implemented here". This dead surface also keeps the v1 proto compilation alive (see the proto-duplication finding).
findings.recommendation: Once grpc-signer's connect path moves to v2 (ISSUE-1.9), delete the v1 trait impl, lib.rs v1 exports, v1 tests, and the audit compat re-exports in one PR; re-introduce a v1-style listener only if ADR-010's insecure listener is ever actually built.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: SigningGateError → status/body sanitization policy duplicated between gRPC and HTTP mappers
findings.detail: `gate_err_to_status` (service.rs:399-432) and `gate_err_to_http` + `audit_label` (response.rs:59-113) implement the same policy twice: identical category splits (slashable-violation detail is safe to surface; other DB errors are logged server-side and replaced with a generic string), identical message strings ("slashing protection violation: {inner}", "slashing DB commit failed; same-root retry is safe", "internal signing error", "unknown public key") and identical `tracing::error!` sites. response.rs's module doc explicitly acknowledges it "reuses the error categories and sanitization rules" of the gRPC table — by re-typing them. Adding a SigningGateError variant now requires synchronized edits in two mappers plus audit_label.
findings.recommendation: Add one shared classification, e.g. `fn classify(e: &SigningGateError) -> (GateErrClass, Cow<str>)` (in crates/signer next to the error type, or in the bin), where GateErrClass ∈ {SlashingViolation, SlashingDbError, CommitFailed, KeyNotFound, SigningFailed, Doppelganger}; derive tonic Status codes, HTTP status codes, and audit labels from the class in thin per-transport tables.
findings.scope: bin/rvc-signer — standalone gRPC/HTTP remote BLS signing server (~15.6k src + ~3.7k tests LOC)

findings.title: Two parallel safe-signing stacks in crates/signer with divergent safety features
findings.detail: The crate contains two complete, independently-maintained implementations of the same lock -> doppelganger-gate -> stage -> sign -> commit/discard flow: SignerService (lib.rs, used by the VC via bin/rvc, block-service, builder) and SigningGate (gate.rs, used only by bin/rvc-signer). Each has features the other lacks: SigningGate wraps the BLS sign in a 4s tokio timeout (BUG-003 fix, gate.rs:101,286) and uses PubkeyScopedDb for audit-CN + GVR pinning (gate.rs:272); SignerService has no sign timeout at all (lib.rs:386 `handle.block_on(signer.sign(...))` unbounded), but has the metrics instrumentation (RVC_SIGNER_SLASHING_TX_HOLD_DURATION_MS, RVC_SLASHING_PROTECTION_CHECKS_TOTAL) and the re-check-enablement-under-lock step (lib.rs:303) that SigningGate lacks. sign_attestation and sign_block inside SignerService are themselves ~150-line near-verbatim copies of each other, as are the pair in SigningGate. Any future fix (e.g. a new timeout policy or metric) must be hand-ported to 4 sites.
findings.recommendation: Extract one internal slashable-signing core: fn sign_slashable(stage_fn, signing_root, pubkey, hooks) that owns the spawn_blocking + Handle::block_on(timeout(...)) + commit/discard pattern, parameterized by a metrics/tracing hook so both entry points share it. Then make SignerService delegate to SigningGate (or the shared core) so the timeout, PubkeyScopedDb auditing, and metrics exist on both paths. The 4 near-identical slashable methods collapse to 2 thin wrappers.
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: Domain/signing-root derivation duplicated across three layers; EIP-7044 cap implemented four times
findings.detail: The epoch -> ForkName::from_epoch -> fork_version -> compute_domain -> compute_signing_root sequence is re-implemented per duty type in at least three live layers: (1) each of SignerService's 10 methods in crates/signer/src/lib.rs inlines it; (2) each of LocalSigner's 10 TypedSigner methods in typed_signer.rs inlines it; (3) each Web3Signer request builder in remote_signer.rs (build_attestation_request etc.) inlines it again. The 130-line MockGrpcSigner in composite_signer.rs tests re-implements all 10 of them a fourth time because there is no shared helper to reuse. The EIP-7044 Capella cap for voluntary exits exists verbatim in four places: signer/src/lib.rs:930-934, crypto/voluntary_exit_signing.rs:23, crypto/typed_signer.rs:330-334 (capella_capped_fork_version), and bin/rvc-keygen/src/exit.rs:127 — a fork-schedule bug fix would need four synchronized edits, and typed_signer's sign_voluntary_exit relies on a documented caller obligation (typed_signer.rs:129-143) instead of applying the cap itself.
findings.recommendation: Add one per-duty signing-root module in crypto (e.g. fn signing_root_for(duty: DutyMessage, ctx: &SignContext) -> Root, plus a fork-schedule-aware variant) and have SignerService, the TypedSigner impls, the Web3Signer request builders, and test mocks all call it. Apply the Capella cap inside that single function (delete capella_capped_fork_version call-sites and the caller-obligation doc). Consider a blanket `impl<T: RawSigner> TypedSigner for T` so LocalSigner's 150-line typed impl and test mocks disappear entirely.
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: crypto is a god-crate: generic logging/redaction utilities force 20 crates to depend on BLS/HTTP/KDF stack
findings.detail: crypto::logging (TruncatedPubkey, TruncatedRoot, RedactedUrl, request IDs, log sampling, span-field helpers, Duty field enum, a conformance module) is imported by ~20 crates including beacon, bn-manager, slashing, doppelganger, validator-store, propagator and secret-provider — crates that need only log formatting but now transitively pull blst, reqwest, scrypt, aes, rayon, bip39, hkdf, num-bigint, uuid (crypto/Cargo.toml deps). These edges are absent from the ARCHITECTURE.md dependency graph (it shows no BNM->CRYPTO or BEACON->CRYPTO edge), so the documented layering has silently eroded: a 'foundation' crate for cryptography is functioning as the workspace commons. Additionally remote_signer.rs:54-64 (redact_url) duplicates logging::RedactedUrl verbatim inside the same crate.
findings.recommendation: Extract a dependency-light foundation crate (e.g. crates/observability or crates/logging) holding logging.rs, hex.rs, and CanonicalPubkey (pubkey.rs); repoint the ~20 dependents at it and drop their crypto dependency where logging was the only use. Delete the private redact_url in remote_signer.rs in favor of RedactedUrl. Update the ARCHITECTURE.md graph after the move — it will become accurate again for free.
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: crates/signer/src/lib.rs is a 3,008-line god-file: service, errors, enablement types, and a 1,670-line inline test harness
findings.detail: lib.rs holds SignerService with 10 sign methods, SignerError, FailClosedEnablement, AlwaysEnabled, truncate_error_body, sampling statics, the 200-line ValidatorSigner trait impl, and from line 1338 a ~1,670-line #[cfg(test)] module that includes a bespoke tracing-capture harness (CapturedEvent/CapturedSpan/Capture layer, ValueVisitor/EventVisitor). The 7 non-slashable methods (sign_randao_reveal:627, sign_sync_committee_message:680, sign_selection_proof:732, sign_aggregate_and_proof:786, sign_electra_aggregate_and_proof:841, sign_voluntary_exit:907, sign_builder_registration:969, sign_sync_committee_selection_proof:1016, sign_contribution_and_proof:1073) are ~60-line copies differing only in domain constant, message type, and the signing_type string — gate.rs already demonstrates the right shape with its single sign_nonslashable helper (gate.rs:529) that all 7 wrappers call.
findings.recommendation: Split lib.rs: service.rs (SignerService), enablement.rs (FailClosedEnablement/AlwaysEnabled), keep error types in error.rs. Introduce a sign_nonslashable-style private helper mirroring gate.rs so the 7 non-slashable methods become 3-line wrappers. Move the inline test module (and its tracing-capture harness) into tests/ or a tests submodule file, and share the harness with the integration tests instead of keeping it private to lib.rs.
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: Error taxonomy is fragmented and SignerService conflates commit failure with slashing rejection
findings.detail: The same failure space has two unreconciled enums: SignerError (lib.rs:48, used by the VC path) and SigningGateError (error.rs, used by rvc-signer). SigningGateError carefully distinguishes BlockedBySlashingDb (slot consumed, do NOT retry with a different root) from SlashingDbCommitFailed (nothing written, same-root retry safe) — the doc comments at error.rs:18-45 explain the retry semantics are opposite. SignerService, however, maps a commit failure to SignerError::SlashingProtectionBlocked (lib.rs:395-405 and 558-568), so VC-side callers cannot distinguish 'genuinely slashable, never retry' from 'I/O hiccup, retry is safe'. Additionally, crypto's SigningError lives in signer_trait.rs rather than error.rs, SignerError stringifies signer errors (SigningFailed(String)) losing the source chain, and truncate_error_body is an ad-hoc helper in lib.rs.
findings.recommendation: Converge on one signing error enum (or make SignerError a thin re-mapping of SigningGateError) with distinct SlashingBlocked vs CommitFailed variants carrying #[source] SlashingError; fix the SignerService commit-failure arms to use the CommitFailed variant. Move SigningError from signer_trait.rs into crypto/src/error.rs so the crate's error taxonomy is in one place.
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: Legacy dead signing API surface in crypto: free SecretKey-based sign functions, RawSigner, and a shadowed domain constant
findings.detail: crypto exports ~10 free functions that sign with a raw &SecretKey (sign_attestation, sign_block, sign_randao_reveal, sign_sync_committee_message, sign_contribution_and_proof, sign_aggregate_and_proof, sign_electra_aggregate_and_proof, sign_selection_proof, sign_builder_registration, sign_sync_committee_selection_proof). Workspace-wide search shows no production caller outside crypto except sign_voluntary_exit (bin/rvc-keygen/src/exit.rs) and is_aggregator (re-exported by signer, used by the orchestrator) — every duty path goes through SignerService/SigningGate/TypedSigner instead. These functions bypass CompositeSigner and slashing protection by design, which crates/signer/tests/no_direct_composite_signer_outside_signer.rs:60-62 explicitly polices against. The RawSigner trait (typed_signer.rs:32) is exported but has zero users outside its own file. signing.rs:8 redefines DOMAIN_BEACON_ATTESTER even though eth_types already exports it (crypto imports the eth_types one elsewhere, e.g. typed_signer.rs:12).
findings.recommendation: Delete the unused free sign_* functions and the RawSigner trait; keep compute_domain/compute_signing_root, is_aggregator, and a single voluntary-exit helper for rvc-keygen (or port keygen to TypedSigner on a LocalSigner). Replace the local DOMAIN_BEACON_ATTESTER with the eth_types constant. Their extensive tests (fork-boundary, KATs) should migrate to the surviving signing-root helper rather than be dropped.
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: KeyManager has two duplicated directory loaders with divergent security behavior; the tracker variant is production-dead
findings.detail: load_from_directory_with_threads_filtered (line 110) and load_from_directory_with_tracker (line 376) duplicate the ~110-line directory-scan loop, and the copies have drifted: the tracker variant skips the validate_key_path traversal check (lines 396-414 iterate entries with no canonicalization), performs no declared-vs-derived pubkey verification (the parallel path rejects mismatches at lines 300-311), and logs full untruncated pubkeys (lines 437, 463 use %pubkey_hex where the rest of the crate uses TruncatedPubkey). load_from_directory_with_tracker and DecryptionAttemptTracker have no callers outside key_manager.rs tests and decryption_tracker.rs itself — the only production loader call is crates/rvc/src/config/builder.rs:301 using the filtered variant — yet ARCHITECTURE.md advertises DecryptionAttemptTracker as a live feature.
findings.recommendation: Either delete load_from_directory_with_tracker + DecryptionAttemptTracker (and correct ARCHITECTURE.md), or fold rate-limit tracking into the single 3-phase pipeline as an optional parameter so there is exactly one scan loop with the traversal check, pubkey verification, and truncated logging applied uniformly.
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: ValidatorSigner trait returns Vec<u8>, forcing a 200-line delegation impl and duplicate method surface
findings.detail: ValidatorSigner (traits.rs) mirrors SignerService's 10 inherent methods but returns Vec<u8> instead of crypto::Signature, so lib.rs:1137-1336 is 200 lines of pure boilerplate: each trait method calls the identically-named inherent method and appends .to_bytes().to_vec(). Every new duty type must be added in three places (trait, inherent impl, delegation impl). The trait is also #[async_trait(?Send)], which prevents holding it across spawns and is one reason sibling crates grow their own signer traits (e.g. sync-service defines its own SyncSigner: Send + Sync at crates/sync-service/src/lib.rs:28 instead of reusing ValidatorSigner).
findings.recommendation: Change ValidatorSigner to return crypto::Signature (callers can call to_bytes() at the wire boundary), implement it directly on SignerService, and delete the parallel inherent methods (or keep them and derive the trait impl with a small macro). Evaluate dropping ?Send so domain crates like sync-service can share the trait instead of defining private ones.
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: Web3Signer wire contract types are hand-mirrored between the crypto client and the rvc-signer server
findings.detail: remote_signer.rs defines the serialize side of the Web3Signer contract (WireForkInfo, Web3SignerPayload with 10 type-tagged variants, Web3SignerSignRequest) and its own comment states 'Shape mirrors bin/rvc-signer/src/http_api/request.rs (read-only reference)' — the server defines the deserialize twin (WireForkInfo at request.rs:30, SignPayload at request.rs:80) as an independent set of types kept in sync only by convention and contract tests. Both sides also duplicate the type_name() discriminator match (remote_signer.rs:223-241 vs request.rs:136-150). remote_signer.rs itself is 1,551 lines mixing URL gating, config, wire types, 11 request builders, the HTTP client, Signer + TypedSigner impls, and ~800 lines of tests.
findings.recommendation: Extract the wire types into one shared module with both Serialize and Deserialize derives (a small web3signer-wire crate, or a module in crypto the server imports) so client and server cannot drift, and split remote_signer.rs into wire.rs (types + builders) and client.rs (RemoteSigner HTTP + trait impls).
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: signer integration tests re-implement enablement mocks and gate builders in 13 files while the crate's own test-helpers go unused
findings.detail: Each of the 13+ gate test files defines its own AlwaysAllowed/AlwaysDenied SigningEnablement struct and a make_gate*/make_signer_with_key builder that constructs KeyManager -> LocalSigner -> CompositeSigner -> SigningGate (e.g. gate_attestation_happy_path.rs:19-48 vs gate_block_doppelganger_blocked.rs:17-27, near-identical). Meanwhile the crate already ships AlwaysEnabled/always_enabled() behind the test-helpers feature (lib.rs:152-169) which its own tests never use. Several files hold a single test each (gate_attestation_doppelganger_blocked.rs 64 lines, gate_block_doppelganger_blocked.rs 62, log_sampling_disabled.rs 54), each paying separate link/compile cost as its own integration-test binary.
findings.recommendation: Add tests/common/mod.rs with the enablement mocks and a gate_fixture() builder; consolidate the one-test doppelganger-blocked files into a single gate_doppelganger.rs and the log-sampling pair into one file. Point the mocks at the existing test-helpers items (or delete those helpers if the common module supersedes them).
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: Redundant re-export modules and colliding crate names blur the signer crate's public surface
findings.detail: slashable.rs and non_slashable.rs are 20/25-line doc-only modules whose sole content is `pub use crate::gate::SigningGate;` — the same type is now reachable as signer::SigningGate, signer::slashable::SigningGate, and signer::non_slashable::SigningGate, and their module docs restate (and can drift from) gate.rs's own docs. Separately, the library package in crates/signer is named rvc-signer while the binary in bin/rvc-signer is package rvc-signer-bin producing a binary named rvc-signer; code says `use rvc_signer::...` for the lib, and grep/log output for 'rvc-signer' is ambiguous between the two. The signing vocabulary also spans Signer, RawSigner, TypedSigner, LocalSigner, RemoteSigner, CompositeSigner, GrpcRemoteSigner, ValidatorSigner, SignerService, SigningGate — with no doc that maps the hierarchy.
findings.recommendation: Delete the slashable/non_slashable re-export modules, moving any unique doc content onto the gate methods. Rename the library package (e.g. rvc-signing or rvc-safe-signer) or the binary package to remove the collision. Add a short module-level doc in crypto/src/lib.rs mapping the signer-trait hierarchy (raw vs typed vs composite vs service/gate).
findings.scope: crates/crypto + crates/signer (BLS, keystores, Web3Signer client, safe-signing layer)

findings.title: EIP-3076 rule logic exists in three parallel copies and has already drifted: the production stage_* path missed the watermark-equality fix
findings.detail: The double-vote/surround/surrounded/min-target/watermark checks are hand-written three times for attestations (is_safe_to_sign db.rs:977-1035, check_and_record_attestation db.rs:1548-1714, stage_attestation stage.rs:481-618) and three times for blocks (is_safe_to_propose, check_and_record_block, stage_block). The copies have drifted: commit 40b6c1e ('watermark equality... use <= per EIP-3076 equality blocking') changed the target-watermark and block-watermark comparisons from < to <= in db.rs only (db.rs:969, 1276, 1377, 1582 all use <=, with 'SEC-9 / M-1' comments), while stage.rs:356 still uses '(slot as i64) < wm' and stage.rs:506 still uses '(target_epoch as i64) < wt'. stage_block/stage_attestation are the only production signing path (called via crates/signer/src/gate.rs:275/410, crates/signer/src/lib.rs:351/529, bin/rvc-signer/src/dvt/peer_service.rs:261/394) — so the fix landed everywhere except where it matters. tests/stage.rs has no watermark test, so nothing catches the divergence.
findings.recommendation: Extract one pure rule-evaluation core, e.g. fn check_attestation(existing_rows, watermarks, candidate, strict) -> Result<Outcome, AttestationSlashingViolation> and a block equivalent in a new src/rules.rs, with all six entry points delegating to it (they differ only in transaction plumbing and log level). Immediately align stage.rs to <= and add stage-path watermark-equality tests. This collapses ~400 duplicated lines and makes future rule fixes single-site.
findings.scope: crates/slashing — EIP-3076 slashing protection (SQLite), ~10.9k LOC

findings.title: Two dead generations of check/record APIs remain public; only stage_* is used in production
findings.detail: rg across the workspace shows every non-slashing-crate caller of is_safe_to_sign, is_safe_to_propose, record_attestation, record_block, check_and_record_block and check_and_record_attestation sits inside #[cfg(test)] modules (crates/signer/src/lib.rs:1883 and :2904 are both inside the test module starting at line 1338; crates/rvc/src/keymanager_adapters.rs:2708, doppelganger_adapter.rs:124, config/builder.rs:1018 are all tests). db.rs:1334-1339 even documents this: 'today it has no non-test callers'. check_and_record_* additionally carries a dead `_client_cn` parameter kept only 'for call-site compatibility with the... test harness' (db.rs:1325), and check_and_record_attestation has its FU-32/FU-33 doc block copy-pasted twice (db.rs:1468-1490 and 1491-1521). Maintaining three public generations of the most safety-critical logic is the direct cause of the drift in the previous finding.
findings.recommendation: Delete generation 1 (is_safe_to_* + record_*) or demote it to pub(crate) test helpers; either delete check_and_record_* or reimplement it as a thin stage+commit wrapper (stage_block(...)?.commit()) so only one rule path exists. Drop the _client_cn parameter and the duplicated doc block. Port the affected tests to stage_* as part of the migration.
findings.scope: crates/slashing — EIP-3076 slashing protection (SQLite), ~10.9k LOC

findings.title: EIP-3076 conformance and property-test suites exercise the non-production code path
findings.detail: The 76-case official conformance suite (tests/conformance.rs) drives db.check_and_record_block/attestation, and the property tests (tests/proptest_slashing.rs:49-123) do the same — but production signing goes exclusively through stage_block/stage_attestation + commit.
