The production path is covered only by 16 narrower unit tests in tests/stage.rs, none of which touch watermarks. This is exactly why the stage-path watermark-equality regression went unnoticed: the heavyweight test artillery validates a path with zero production callers.
findings.recommendation: Point the conformance and proptest runners at the staged API (stage_*(...) then commit()/discard()), or at the extracted shared rule core once it exists, so the certified behavior is the behavior that ships. Keep one thin smoke test on check_and_record_* only if that API survives the previous finding.
findings.scope: crates/slashing — EIP-3076 slashing protection (SQLite), ~10.9k LOC

findings.title: db.rs is a 5,466-line god-file; 61% is two inline test modules, and schema migrations are split inconsistently between db.rs and migration.rs
findings.detail: db.rs mixes at least six concerns in one impl block (lines 81-2120): file preflight/chmod/pragmas (open, preflight_path, chmod_*, configure_pragmas), v1→v2 migration (migrate_to_v2, run_v2_migration_transaction at 644-760) while the v3 migration lives in a separate migration.rs — so half the migration story is inline and half is not, and migration.rs:26-33 re-implements read_schema_version that already exists at db.rs:515; CRUD reads; the EIP-3076 check methods; interchange import/export (1057-1213); watermarks/prune (1832-2031); and metadata/GVR-cache logic. On top of that sit two #[cfg(test)] modules spanning lines 2122-5466 (~3,340 lines, 168 tests). Navigating or reviewing changes to the safety-critical check logic requires scrolling past unrelated file-permission and backup code.
findings.recommendation: Split into a db/ module directory: open.rs (preflight, pragmas, permissions, backup), migrations.rs (absorb migration.rs plus migrate_to_v2, sharing read_schema_version/column_exists), checks.rs (or the shared rules.rs from finding 1), interchange.rs (import/export + read_* snapshot helpers), watermarks.rs (watermark get/set + prune). Move each test cluster next to the code it tests. Pure code motion — no behavior change.
findings.scope: crates/slashing — EIP-3076 slashing protection (SQLite), ~10.9k LOC

findings.title: The entire watermark/prune subsystem is unreachable from production code
findings.detail: rg over the whole workspace finds zero non-test callers of set_block_watermark, set_attestation_watermark, get_*_watermark or prune_below_watermarks — neither bin/rvc nor bin/rvc-signer wires them (no CLI subcommand, no periodic task). Consequently: (a) the RVC_SLASHING_DB_PRUNE_TOTAL metric (db.rs:2012-2017) can never increment; (b) the watermark queries executed on every single sign in all three check paths (e.g. stage.rs:348-362, 482-512) always return None in production; (c) four error variants (WatermarkLowered, NoWatermarksSet, BelowBlockWatermark, BelowAttestation*Watermark) are unreachable; (d) ARCHITECTURE.md advertises 'Pruning — Watermark-based pruning' as a shipped feature. The code is tested but nothing drives it.
findings.recommendation: Decide the feature's fate: either wire it up (set watermarks from interchange maxima on import — the 'minimal' strategy the conformance suite simulates by hand with HashMaps — and add a periodic prune task or `rvc prune` subcommand), or delete the subsystem and its per-sign queries. Half-built infrastructure on the hottest path is the worst of both options.
findings.scope: crates/slashing — EIP-3076 slashing protection (SQLite), ~10.9k LOC

findings.title: genesis_validators_root is stringly-typed with three inconsistent textual encodings across metadata, rows, and interchange
findings.detail: GVR crosses the API as &str in set_genesis_validators_root/export/import but as &Root in stage_*/record_*/check_and_record_*. The textual forms diverge: startup pins metadata as 'lowercase, no 0x prefix' (startup.rs comment at 114-116); runtime inserts write root_to_hex (0x-prefixed lowercase, db.rs:377-379); import() writes the caller's raw config string verbatim into every row (db.rs:1148 'let gvr_hex = expected_genesis_validators_root.to_owned()') and compares interchange metadata by exact string equality (db.rs:1136), so a case or 0x-prefix difference spuriously rejects an import. Because the v3 unique indexes compare gvr as TEXT ((pubkey, genesis_validators_root, target_epoch)), import-written rows and runtime-written rows for the same chain can carry different gvr strings and silently escape the uniqueness backstop. Only the M-6 check normalizes properly (parse_gvr_hex accepts both forms).
findings.recommendation: Introduce a CanonicalGvr newtype mirroring crypto::pubkey::CanonicalPubkey (the crate already cites that pattern as 'the single source of truth' for pubkeys, db.rs:49-51): parse once at the boundary, one canonical encoding (0x-prefixed lowercase) for metadata rows, per-row columns, and interchange comparison. Change import/export/set_genesis_validators_root to take the typed value.
findings.scope: crates/slashing — EIP-3076 slashing protection (SQLite), ~10.9k LOC

findings.title: Per-sign attestation checks load the validator's entire signing history into memory, and nothing bounds its growth
findings.detail: All three attestation check paths run 'SELECT source_epoch, target_epoch, signing_root FROM attestations WHERE pubkey = ?1' with no LIMIT and collect into a Vec, then loop in Rust (stage.rs:514-530 on the production path). A validator attests once per epoch (~82k rows/year), and since pruning is never invoked (previous finding), every sign scans and materializes an ever-growing history while holding the global connection mutex — the same mutex held across the signer call by the staged guard (stage.rs module docs, lines 32-48), so scan time directly extends the signing critical section for all validators.
findings.recommendation: Replace the row loop with targeted SQL under the same transaction: unique-index lookup for the double-vote/target-epoch case, one EXISTS query each for surrounding and surrounded (WHERE source_epoch > ?new_source AND target_epoch < ?new_target and the inverse), and MIN(target_epoch) for the minimum check — all O(log n) via the existing indexes. Alternatively, wiring up pruning caps n; doing both is cheapest to reason about.
findings.scope: crates/slashing — EIP-3076 slashing protection (SQLite), ~10.9k LOC

findings.title: Watermark SQL literal and read-check-upsert pattern repeated 15 times with magic-string type keys
findings.detail: "SELECT value FROM watermarks WHERE pubkey = ?1 AND watermark_type = '...'" appears verbatim 12 times in db.rs and 3 times in stage.rs, keyed by the magic strings 'block', 'att_source', 'att_target'. set_block_watermark and set_attestation_watermark also duplicate the read-then-raise-or-insert dance (db.rs:1832-1863 vs 1882-1938), with set_block_watermark using UPDATE-or-INSERT while set_attestation_watermark uses ON CONFLICT upsert — two idioms for the same operation.
findings.recommendation: Add a WatermarkKind enum with an as_str() and two helpers on a caller-held connection: read_watermark(conn, pubkey, kind) -> Result<Option<i64>> and raise_watermark(tx, pubkey, kind, value) using the ON CONFLICT form. All 15 call sites collapse; typos in a magic string become compile errors.
findings.scope: crates/slashing — EIP-3076 slashing protection (SQLite), ~10.9k LOC

findings.title: SlashingError::MigrationError is a dead duplicate of MigrationFailed
findings.detail: error.rs defines both MigrationError(String) ('migration error: {0}') and MigrationFailed(String) ('schema migration failed: {0}'). Every construction site in the crate (db.rs, migration.rs) uses MigrationFailed exclusively; MigrationError is only fabricated inside test modules in bin/rvc-signer/src/http_api/response.rs (test module starts at line 161) as a stand-in generic DB error. Downstream code must reason about both (bin/rvc-signer/src/service.rs:410 comments 'DatabaseError, MigrationError, etc.'), for a variant that can never occur.
findings.recommendation: Delete MigrationError, switch the two rvc-signer tests to MigrationFailed (or DatabaseError), and keep MigrationFailed as the single migration-failure variant.
findings.scope: crates/slashing — EIP-3076 slashing protection (SQLite), ~10.9k LOC

findings.title: SlashingDbReader re-implements MAX(target_epoch) in Rust over a full row fetch
findings.detail: reader.rs:80-81 implements last_signed_attestation by calling get_attestations(pubkey) — which materializes every attestation row for the validator — and then computing .map(|a| a.target_epoch).max() in Rust, while SlashingDb::last_signed_attestation_epoch (db.rs:1745-1760) already does exactly this with 'SELECT MAX(target_epoch) ... WHERE pubkey = ?1' against the covering index. The doppelganger crate calls this on startup for every monitored validator.
findings.recommendation: Have the SlashingDbReader impl delegate to self.last_signed_attestation_epoch(pubkey) after the existing pinned-GVR gate, deleting the manual max fold and the full-history fetch.
findings.scope: crates/slashing — EIP-3076 slashing protection (SQLite), ~10.9k LOC

findings.title: Four copy-pasted retry/status-handling loops in BeaconClient (~500 lines)
findings.detail: client.rs contains four nearly identical ~130-line retry loops: submit_attestation (759-900), execute_with_retry (902-1032), post_empty_with_headers (1035-1160), and execute_with_retry_raw (1163-1279). Each repeats verbatim the same status ladder: success path, 429 with Retry-After backoff, 4xx immediate return with read_body_capped_lossy, 5xx retry, timeout retry, connect-error retry, and the final 'retries exhausted' error/span logging. submit_attestation exists only to special-case 400 partial-failure parsing yet re-implements the entire loop, including two match arms (795-818) whose bodies are byte-identical. Any change to backoff, 429 handling, or logging must be made four times; the 429 handling in submit_attestation already logs slightly differently from the others.
findings.recommendation: Make execute_with_retry_raw the single retry engine (it already returns the raw Response). Rebuild execute_with_retry as raw + read_body_capped + serde parse, post_empty_with_headers as raw + discard body, and submit_attestation as raw with a small on_client_error hook (or a status-interceptor closure) for the 400 partial-failure case. This deletes roughly 350 lines and gives one place to tune retry semantics.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: Monolithic 26-method BeaconNodeClient trait forces ~11 hand-rolled mocks and a fallible default-impl footgun
findings.detail: BeaconNodeClient bundles all 26 beacon operations into one trait. rg shows 11 files with `impl BeaconNodeClient for` (15 impls total), and every test mock must stub all ~26 methods with Err(HttpError("mock")) boilerplate (e.g. traits.rs:525-664, aggregation.rs:598-669 — each ~130 lines). The pain is already visible in the code: post_validator_liveness (traits.rs:156-163) was given a default impl that returns an error at runtime explicitly 'so existing test mocks need not implement this method' — meaning a production impl that forgets to override it compiles fine and fails at runtime. Consumers like propagator need exactly one method; builder needs two.
findings.recommendation: Two complementary steps: (1) ship one shared mock (a `test-utils` feature in bn-manager exposing a MockBeaconNodeClient with overridable closures, or adopt mockall) and delete the per-crate hand mocks; (2) remove the error-returning default impl of post_validator_liveness so implementors are forced to decide. Optionally split the trait into role-focused supertraits (DutyFetch, BlockProduction, Submission, NodeStatus) with `BeaconNodeClient: DutyFetch + ...` so domain crates can depend on the narrow capability they use.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: client.rs (75% tests) and manager.rs (62% tests) are giant single files
findings.detail: beacon/src/client.rs is 5357 lines, of which ~4045 (lines 1312-5357, 127 tests) are an inline #[cfg(test)] module dominated by wiremock MockServer integration-style tests. bn-manager/src/manager.rs is 3716 lines with ~2315 lines of inline tests (from line 1402), also wiremock-based. CLAUDE.md's own convention says unit tests go at the bottom of the file but integration tests belong in tests/ — spinning up an HTTP mock server is squarely the latter. The production code you actually need to read (the client's 38 endpoint methods, the manager's strategy engine) is buried, and editors/reviews pay the cost of 4-5k-line files.
findings.recommendation: Move the wiremock-driven test bodies to crates/beacon/tests/client_http.rs and crates/bn-manager/tests/manager_strategies.rs (both crates already have tests/ directories with this pattern, e.g. beacon/tests/body_cap_h12.rs). Keep only true unit tests (calculate_backoff, config builders, parse helpers) inline. This halves both files without touching production code.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: Broadcast-vs-query_first topic dispatch copy-pasted five times in BnManager
findings.detail: publish_block (920-944), publish_blinded_block (946-973), submit_attestation (997-1023), submit_sync_committee_messages (1068-1094), and submit_beacon_committee_subscriptions (1162-1188) each repeat the identical shape: `if self.broadcast_topics.X { with_op_timeout(name, timeout, broadcast(name, op)) } else { with_op_timeout(name, timeout, query_first(name, role, tier, op)) }`, duplicating the op name string three times per method and the whole closure twice. Adding a topic or changing fallback tier means editing five near-identical blocks.
findings.recommendation: Add one private helper, e.g. `async fn submit(&self, op_name, topic_enabled: bool, role, tier, timeout_sel, op) -> Result<T>` that owns the if/else and timeout wrapping; each trait method becomes a 3-5 line call. Also consider deriving fallback role/tier per topic in one table so the policy ('submissions accept LargeLag') is stated once.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: Fallback semantics scattered across layers: retries disabled in BnManager but enabled in parallel single-client paths, and proposer path bypasses failover entirely
findings.detail: BnManager::new hardcodes `.with_max_retries(0)` on every per-BN client (manager.rs:101) — retry responsibility moves up to failover — so the beacon crate's whole retry machinery is dead on the multi-BN path. Meanwhile ConfigBuilder::build_beacon (builder.rs:208-221) constructs a separate raw BeaconClient with `.with_max_retries(3)`, so the process runs two BN access paths with different retry policies. Worst, bin/rvc/src/main.rs:1542-1560 builds the block-production client by taking `proposer_nodes[0]` and wrapping a fresh BeaconClient with max_retries(0) — the comment admits 'we need an Arc<BeaconClient> but proposer_mgr is an Arc<BnManager>' — so when proposer nodes are configured, block production has neither retries nor multi-BN failover, precisely the duty that needs them most.
findings.recommendation: Make the retry/failover split an explicit policy: BeaconClientConfig used by BnManager should state retries=0 in one documented place, and BeaconBlockAdapter should accept `Arc<dyn BeaconNodeClient>` (or the proposer BnManager itself) instead of Arc<BeaconClient> so the proposer path goes through failover. Remove or narrow build_beacon so only exit-command tooling uses raw clients.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: 165-line manual passthrough impl of BeaconNodeClient for BeaconClient
findings.detail: manager.rs:1238-1400 implements BeaconNodeClient for BeaconClient with 26 methods that each do nothing but delegate to the inherent method of the same name (`self.get_genesis().await`, etc.). Every new endpoint added to the trait requires touching: the BeaconClient inherent method, the trait, this passthrough impl, the BnManager impl, and every test mock — five places for one endpoint (the current cost of the 'endpoint-method sprawl').
findings.recommendation: Generate the passthrough with a small declarative macro (list of `fn name(args) -> Ret` entries expanding both the trait and the delegating impl), or use the `delegate` crate. Combined with the shared-mock finding, adding an endpoint then touches two places instead of five.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: Dead configuration and always-empty fields in bn-manager
findings.detail: Several knobs exist but are never read by production code: (1) BnSelectionStrategy and BnManagerConfig.selection_strategy (traits.rs:200, 232) are never referenced in manager.rs — strategy is hardcoded per endpoint method — yet the field is publicly configurable and tested; (2) BnHealthScore.head_slot is hardwired to None in health_scores() (manager.rs:194) while tests assert Some values; (3) ResponseCaps.max_sse_event_bytes (http_caps.rs:18) is unused outside its own module — sse.rs defines its own DEFAULT_MAX_SSE_EVENT_BYTES with the same 64 KiB value, and BnManager::start_sse (manager.rs:240) builds SseConfig::new without wiring any cap from BnManagerConfig; (4) BnOutcome.latency is #[allow(dead_code)] (broadcast.rs:10). Each is a trap: a user setting selection_strategy=Best gets silently ignored.
findings.recommendation: Delete BnSelectionStrategy and the selection_strategy field (strategy is per-operation by design — document that on BnManager instead), drop head_slot or populate it from BnSyncDetail, remove ResponseCaps.max_sse_event_bytes and make sse.rs's constant the single source (or wire a cap through BnManagerConfig into start_sse), and remove the dead latency field or use it in log_partial_failure.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: Stringly-typed beacon API structs duplicate eth-types and push parsing into consumers
findings.detail: beacon/src/types.rs defines its own Checkpoint, AttestationData, AttesterDuty, ProposerDuty, BeaconCommitteeSubscription, ProposerPreparation etc. with every numeric field as String (`slot: String`, `epoch: String`, `validator_index: String`), while eth-types already provides typed equivalents (eth-types/src/lib.rs:95-103 has Checkpoint/AttestationData) with quoted-int serde specifically for API compatibility (per ARCHITECTURE.md). The string types leak through bn-manager's re-exports into rvc, which then hand-parses: utils.rs:14/34 `duty.committee_length.parse()`, coordinator.rs:631 `proposer_duty.validator_index.parse::<u64>()`, each with bespoke error branches. Two parallel AttestationData types with the same name across crates also invites confusion (propagator tests import bn_manager::AttestationData, crypto uses eth_types').
findings.recommendation: Migrate beacon response/request structs to eth-types' typed Slot/Epoch/u64 fields using serde_with quoted-int (the pattern already exists in eth-types), or at minimum replace the duplicated Checkpoint/AttestationData with re-exports of the eth-types versions. Do it endpoint-by-endpoint (duties first, since they have the most downstream parsing). This removes a whole class of parse-and-log-error code in the orchestrator.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: Trace-context header injection boilerplate repeated ~7 times in BeaconClient
findings.detail: The sequence `let mut trace_headers = HeaderMap::new(); telemetry::inject_trace_context(&mut trace_headers); let hdrs = trace_headers.clone();` followed by a `for (name, value) in &hdrs { req = req.header(name.clone(), value.clone()) }` loop appears in get, post, produce_block_v3 (twice, including the JSON fallback at 379-390), publish_block_ssz, submit_attestation, and post_empty_with_headers. produce_block_v3 additionally clones the map a second time (hdrs2) for the fallback request.
findings.recommendation: Add a private helper `fn traced(&self, rb: reqwest::RequestBuilder) -> reqwest::RequestBuilder` (RequestBuilder has `.headers(HeaderMap)` — the manual loop is unnecessary) or inject the headers once inside the consolidated retry engine from the retry-dedup finding, since every request goes through it.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: Propagator crate covers only plain attestations; other submissions bypass it, splitting metrics/error handling
findings.detail: The propagator crate (646 lines incl. tests) exposes a single method, Propagator::propagate, for attestations only. Aggregate proofs are submitted directly via self.beacon.submit_aggregate_and_proofs in the orchestrator (aggregation.rs:382, 430), and sync messages/contributions likewise go straight to BnManager — so the 'message propagation' layer with its RVC_ATTESTATIONS_TOTAL metric accounting and partial-failure classification exists for exactly one of four submission types. The AttestationSubmitter trait plus its blanket impl for all BeaconNodeClient (lib.rs:27-35) adds an indirection layer that any BeaconNodeClient already satisfies, and extract_attestation_context computes a committee index that is immediately discarded (lib.rs:104). PropagationResult's counts also duplicate what the PartialFailure error variant carries.
findings.recommendation: Pick a direction: either extend Propagator to own all four submission paths (uniform metrics, partial-failure logging, one place for submission policy) or fold its ~120 production lines into rvc/src/orchestrator/attestation.rs and delete the crate. If kept, drop the AttestationSubmitter trait in favor of Arc<dyn BeaconNodeClient> (the blanket impl proves they are equivalent) and remove the unused committee-index extraction.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: Per-result write-lock churn in query_best and fallback_unsynced, inconsistent with query_first's batched updates
findings.detail: query_first deliberately batches health-tracker updates ('Batch update: record success + all prior errors in one lock acquisition', manager.rs:412-419), and broadcast_inner does the same (714-742). But query_best_inner acquires self.health_trackers.write().await once per result inside its loop (570, 583), and fallback_unsynced does so per attempt (640, 651). With several BNs this is repeated contended lock acquisition in the hot block-production path, and the inconsistency makes the intended locking discipline unclear.
findings.recommendation: Collect (index, outcome, latency) tuples during the loops and apply them under a single write() guard afterwards, mirroring query_first — or extract a small `record_outcomes(&self, outcomes)` helper used by all four strategies so the discipline is enforced in one place.
findings.scope: beacon HTTP client, bn-manager multi-BN failover, propagator (crates/beacon, crates/bn-manager, crates/propagator)

findings.title: handlers.rs is a 4181-line monolith: 8 endpoint groups plus a 3200-line inline integration-test suite
findings.detail: handlers.rs holds every handler group in one file: keystores, remote keys (line 456), fee recipient (635), gas limit (674), graffiti (710), voluntary exit (743), attesting toggle, plus rate limiters, log-sanitization helpers, and pubkey/address parsers. Lines 980-4181 are a single #[cfg(test)] mod with 103 tests organized into 26 comment-delimited sections (auth middleware, CORS, body limits, SEC-05/06/07, Issue 4.1-4.3 'integration tests') that build full Router/KeymanagerServer instances via tower::ServiceExt::oneshot — this is an integration suite living inside a source file, while 5 more integration files already exist in tests/. The ~300-line mock family (MockKeystoreManager, MockValidatorConfigManager, TestApp with 6 constructor variants) is re-implemented separately in tests/km2_cancel_token_race.rs and tests/post_import_doppelganger_m12.rs (each has its own 48-byte-pubkey mock keystore manager).
findings.recommendation: Split handlers.rs into a handlers/ module tree (keystores.rs, remote_keys.rs, validator_config.rs for fee/gas/graffiti, exits.rs, attesting.rs, common.rs for AppState + parse/sanitize helpers). Move the router-level test sections to tests/ and consolidate the three mock families into one shared harness (tests/common/mod.rs or a test-utils feature exposing TestApp). Keep only true unit tests (parse_pubkey, parse_eth_address, rate-limit logic) in-file per CLAUDE.md.
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: grpc-signer: 10 TypedSigner methods repeat the same ~55-line RPC boilerplate (~550 lines, one varying step each)
findings.detail: Every TypedSigner method in client.rs (sign_block, sign_blinded_block, sign_attestation, sign_aggregate_and_proof, sign_sync_committee_message, sign_sync_aggregator_selection, sign_contribution_and_proof, sign_builder_registration, sign_randao_reveal, sign_voluntary_exit) repeats verbatim: ensure_pubkey → hex::encode pubkey → Self::fork_id → info_span with duty_type → Instant::now → self.client_v2.clone() → RPC call → map_err formatting 'gRPC {method} failed ({code}): {msg}' → latency_ms debug log → compute_domain + compute_signing_root → Self::extract_signature. Only the request struct, the RPC method name, the DOMAIN_* constant, and the signing-root object differ. sign_block additionally logs a request-sent debug line the other nine lack — drift already exists. connect() (lines 117-159) also duplicates the entire channel build + identical 10-line error closures for the TLS and non-TLS branches.
findings.recommendation: Extract a private async helper, e.g. `async fn sign_rpc<R: TreeHash>(&self, duty: &'static str, domain: [u8;4]-producing spec, root_obj: &R, rpc: impl FnOnce(SignerServiceClientV2<Channel>) -> BoxFuture<Result<Response<SignResponse>, Status>>) -> Result<Signature, SigningError>` that owns ensure_pubkey, span, timing, error mapping, domain/root computation and extract_signature; each trait method shrinks to request construction plus one call, and a future RPC cannot forget response-signature verification. In connect(), build the endpoint once and conditionally apply .tls_config() with a single error-mapping closure.
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: Doppelganger import/delete lifecycle state machine is inlined in HTTP handlers around an AppState god-object
findings.detail: AppState (handlers.rs:32-96) mixes 7 injected trait objects with concurrency-critical doppelganger state: cancel_tokens, doppelganger_state_lock, doppelganger_window — documented by 60+ lines of lock-ordering invariants (KM-2, SF-3) that are enforced purely by convention across three code sites: import_keystores inlines ~95 lines of token-displacement + tokio::spawn + select! enable logic (lines 198-293), delete_keystores repeats the lock/cancel discipline (377-399), and the spawned task re-checks cancellation under the same lock. The race-condition tests (tests/km2_cancel_token_race.rs, 661 lines) must drive the full HTTP stack to exercise this. The import paths are also asymmetric: local import registers ValidatorManager + cancel token + enable task, while import_remote_keys (line 513-527) only calls start_monitoring — despite the SEC-2b comment claiming 'the same enablement gate as local imports' — so the lifecycle contract lives in two divergent inline copies.
findings.recommendation: Extract a DoppelgangerLifecycle component (or grow gate.rs, which already owns the window concept) that encapsulates window, cancel_tokens, and the state lock behind on_import(pubkey), on_delete(pubkey), and the background enable task. Handlers become plain request/response mapping; the KM-2 lock-ordering invariant is enforced inside one type; km2_cancel_token_race tests target the component directly instead of the HTTP stack; local vs remote import share one code path with an explicit flag for the ValidatorManager registration difference.
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: secret-provider: boot-load and periodic-refresh are two divergent implementations of the same key-loading pipeline
findings.detail: KeySourceManager::load_all_except and RefreshService::refresh both do list_keys → pubkey_hex denylist precheck → fetch_key → convert_key_material → denylist/known postcheck → collect, but have drifted apart on four axes: (1) the 10-line hex→[u8;48] precheck is copy-pasted (key_source_manager.rs:120-137 vs refresh.rs:78-89); (2) refresh wraps fetch_key in a hardcoded 30s tokio::time::timeout while the boot path has no timeout at all — a hung provider stalls startup indefinitely but not refresh; (3) all RVC_SECRET_PROVIDER_* Prometheus metrics and secret_provider.* OTel spans are only on the boot path — `rg RVC_SECRET_PROVIDER refresh.rs` returns nothing, so recurring refresh failures are invisible to monitoring; (4) boot fetches concurrently via JoinSet, refresh fetches sequentially.
findings.recommendation: Extract one shared instrumented pipeline, e.g. `async fn fetch_provider_keys(provider, denylist: impl Fn(&[u8;48])->bool, timeout: Duration) -> ProviderLoadResult` living in key_source_manager.rs, that owns the hex precheck, timeout, concurrency, metrics, and spans. KeySourceManager and RefreshService then differ only in how they aggregate results (LoadSummary vs new-key list). This closes the observability gap and unifies timeout behavior in one place.
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: Pubkey-hex parsing re-implemented in at least 6 places within/around scope; canonical helper in eth-types goes unused
findings.detail: strip-0x + hex::decode + 48-byte-length-check is hand-rolled in keymanager-api (parse_pubkey), validator-store (parse_hex_bytes), twice inline in secret-provider (key_source_manager.rs:121-126, refresh.rs:79-84), plus rvc/deletion_denylist.rs:159 and bin/rvc-signer/src/http_api/pubkey.rs:47 — while eth-types already exports canonical parse_pubkey_hex (canonical/pubkey_hex.rs:40). The copies have already diverged behaviorally: keymanager-api and secret-provider accept only lowercase '0x', while rvc/keymanager_adapters.rs:179 also handles '0X'; the comment at rvc/orchestrator/attestation.rs:602 documents a past bug caused by exactly this lowercase-only drift.
findings.recommendation: Route all pubkey parsing in these crates through eth-types' parse_pubkey_hex (or add a `Pubkey::from_hex` wrapper there returning [u8;48]) and delete the local copies. validator-store's generic parse_hex_bytes can stay for the 20-byte address case but should delegate the 48-byte case.
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: grpc-signer fork_id duplicates mainnet fork-version constants and silently defaults every unknown network to Deneb
findings.detail: GrpcRemoteSigner::fork_id (client.rs:216-232) matches on raw current_version bytes hardcoding the mainnet values [0x00..]..[0x06..] and falls through to `_ => 4 // default to Deneb` for everything else, per its own comment 'Testnet and devnet fork versions all map to Deneb or latest'. fork_id drives SSZ encoding of blocks/attestations sent to the remote signer (encode_beacon_block_ssz(block, fork_id)), so on Hoodi or any custom network every fork — including Electra — is encoded with the Deneb shape, and each future hard fork requires editing this match. eth-types already owns ForkName/ForkSchedule as the canonical version→fork mapping (per ARCHITECTURE.md), so this is duplicated consensus knowledge with weaker coverage.
findings.recommendation: Carry the resolved ForkName (or the ForkSchedule) in SignContext instead of re-deriving it from raw version bytes, or delegate to an eth-types lookup that accepts the network's fork schedule. At minimum, replace the silent `_ => 4` with a warn!-logged fallback so misclassification on testnets is visible.
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: Stringly-typed error contracts across keymanager-api traits force ad-hoc sanitization at every call site
findings.detail: SlashingProtection::import_interchange/export_interchange return Result<_, String>; ImportRemoteKeyError::Other(String) and DeleteRemoteKeyError::Other(String) are '#[error("{0}")]' passthroughs; url_validator returns Result<url::Url, String>; parse_pubkey returns Result<_, String>. Because the error payloads are opaque strings that may carry paths/sockets/internal names, handlers.rs compensates with sanitize_internal/sanitize_item_err calls sprinkled at each site plus warning comments like 'M-8: DeleteRemoteKeyError::Other passes through whatever the backend put in the inner String... Sanitize' (handlers.rs:606-610). CLAUDE.md prescribes thiserror for library error types.
findings.recommendation: Give SlashingProtection and the remote-key traits real thiserror enums with variants distinguishing client-safe causes (NotFound, InvalidInterchange) from internal ones (Backend(#[source] ...)). Then IntoResponse/one central mapper decides exposure by variant, and the scattered sanitize_* calls collapse to the Internal-variant arm. Same for url_validator (an enum with an is-client-safe Display).
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: KeymanagerServer::new takes 14 positional arguments with clippy::too_many_arguments suppressed
findings.detail: KeymanagerServer::new (server.rs:34-50) takes 7 trait objects + token + addr + cors_origins + body_limit + allow_insecure_remote_signer + attesting_enabled + doppelganger_window as positional parameters under #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]. The production call site (bin/rvc/src/main.rs:1696-1711) and two test call sites (handlers.rs:2635, 2675) each pass 14 positional values; adjacent bool/Duration/usize parameters are transposition-prone and every new setting (the last three were appended for security fixes) grows the signature at all call sites.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a KeymanagerDeps struct (the 7 Arc<dyn ...> objects) and a KeymanagerSettings struct (token, addr, cors_origins, body_limit, allow_insecure_remote_signer, doppelganger_window, attesting_enabled) with Default where sensible; `KeymanagerServer::new(deps, settings)`. Future additions stop touching every call site and field names document intent.
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: sign_voluntary_exit and prepare_exit handlers are copy-paste identical, obscuring whether either submits the exit
findings.detail: The two handlers (handlers.rs:745-767 vs 772-794) have byte-identical bodies — parse pubkey, parse epoch, unwrap exit_manager, call exit_manager.sign_voluntary_exit(&pubkey, epoch) — differing only in the log line. prepare_exit's doc says 'returns it without submitting', but sign_voluntary_exit invokes the exact same trait method, so either both are sign-only (making the /eth/v1 endpoint's implied submit semantics and its 'THIS IS IRREVERSIBLE' warning log misleading) or the differing behavior lives entirely behind the shared VoluntaryExitManager call where it cannot differ.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to one internal fn handle_exit(state, pubkey_hex, query, submit_intent: ExitIntent) with the two routes as thin wrappers, and document (on the VoluntaryExitManager trait) whether signing implies submission. If the endpoints genuinely behave identically today, say so in both route docs or drop the duplicate.
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: validator-store: load_from_config and reload_config duplicate TOML parsing and hardcoded fallback defaults
findings.detail: load_from_config (store.rs:88-138) and reload_config (store.rs:362-415) both read the file, parse TomlConfig, then repeat the same ~25-line block: default fee_recipient=[0u8;20], default gas_limit=30_000_000, optional overrides from [defaults], then per-validator parse_validator loop. The fallback constants appear twice; a future change to one path (e.g. a new defaults field) can silently miss the other, undermining reload_config's parse-first/apply-second guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Extract `fn parse_config(content: &str) -> Result<(ValidatorDefaults, Vec<ValidatorConfig>), ValidatorStoreError>` (with the 30M/zero-address fallbacks defined once as consts) and have both load_from_config and reload_config consume it — load constructs Self, reload applies under the write locks.
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: grpc-signer re-exports the removed v1 raw-root proto client from its public API
findings.detail: lib.rs re-exports the full v1 surface — SignerServiceClient, SignerService/SignerServiceServer, SignRequest/SignResponse, PartialSignRequest/Response (lines 18-23) — with a comment 'kept for the v1 server/trait types used in tests and downstream'. Production code no longer uses it (client.rs:30 notes v1 was removed from the connect path; SS-1/Issue 2.2); the only external consumer found is bin/rvc-signer/tests/tonic_limits_m10.rs, and bin/rvc-signer compiles its own copy of the same proto (bin/rvc-signer/src/proto). Keeping the raw-root SignRequest client in the default public API of the production client crate re-opens the C-2/C-3 oracle path for accidental use — the very thing client.rs's compile-time test exists to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Gate the v1 re-exports behind a non-default feature (e.g. `v1-test-support`) enabled only by the test that needs it, or port tonic_limits_m10.rs to bin/rvc-signer's own proto stubs and delete the v1 module from crates/grpc-signer entirely.
findings.scope: keymanager-api, validator-store, secret-provider, grpc-signer, signer-registry

findings.title: Dual SSZ stacks create seven duplicate public types with identical names
findings.detail: Because ssz_types 0.10.1 implements Encode/Decode only against ethereum_ssz 0.8 while the workspace pins ssz 0.9 (documented in block_body.rs module docs and Cargo.toml comment), block_body.rs redefines Checkpoint, AttestationData, BeaconBlockHeader, DepositData, VoluntaryExit, SignedVoluntaryExit, Attestation, and AttestationElectra as ssz08+TreeHash-derive containers. The root module defines the same eight names as ssz-0.9/serde wire types (lib.rs Checkpoint/AttestationData, block.rs BeaconBlockHeader, deposit.rs DepositData, duties.rs VoluntaryExit/SignedVoluntaryExit, aggregation.rs Attestation/ElectraAttestation). Since `pub mod block_body`, both universes are publicly reachable: `rvc_eth_types::Checkpoint` and `rvc_eth_types::block_body::Checkpoint` are distinct types with identical names, different field types (quoted-u64+hex serde vs none), and different SSZ trait versions. A caller importing the wrong one gets confusing type errors at best; a divergence in field order between the twins would silently change a merkle root at worst.
findings.recommendation: Unify on one ethereum_ssz version (upgrade the workspace ssz to the version ssz_types compiles against, or bump ssz_types when a 0.9-compatible release exists), then collapse each twin into one type. If the version split must stay short-term, stop exposing the duplicates: make block_body's sub-containers pub(crate) where possible, or rename them with an explicit prefix (e.g. WireCheckpoint vs typed Checkpoint) and add a module-level table mapping each twin pair.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: impl_ssz_container! forces every merkleization-sensitive field list to be written twice
findings.detail: block_body.rs invokes impl_ssz_container!($ty { field: type, ... }) 24 times, and each invocation repeats the complete field list of a struct already defined immediately above it (e.g. BeaconBlockBodyElectra's 13 fields appear at lines 613-628 and again at 629-643; ExecutionPayload's 17 fields twice at 450-488). The macro's own doc comment admits the hazard: 'Field order is merkleization- and serialization-sensitive — keep in sync with the struct definition'. Adding a field to a struct but forgetting (or misordering) it in the macro call compiles fine and produces a wrong SSZ encoding/decoding that only a KAT can catch — and only for the vectors that exercise that field.
findings.recommendation: Change the macro to define the struct and the impls from a single field list, e.g. `ssz_container! { #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, TreeHash)] pub struct BeaconBlockBodyElectra { pub randao_reveal: [u8; 96], ... } }` expanding to the struct plus Encode/Decode. This removes ~350 duplicated lines and makes struct/impl divergence unrepresentable.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: Four parallel fork representations with no single conversion point
findings.detail: The workspace juggles four fork encodings: (1) ForkName enum with string names via AsRef<str> (fork.rs:31-43) but no FromStr/parse; (2) BodyForkLayout selected by matching raw consensus_version strings 'deneb'/'electra'/'fulu' in body_fork_layout (block.rs:56-62), a string mapping parallel to ForkName::as_ref; (3) a u32 fork_id (0..=6) validated only by the magic-number check `fork_id > 6` in ssz_helpers.rs:238-243, with the id list re-documented in a comment; (4) grpc-signer/src/client.rs:216-232 re-derives that same u32 by matching hardcoded mainnet version bytes ([0x05,0,0,0] => 5) with a lossy `_ => 4` fallback for testnets. Shipping the next fork requires coordinated edits to ForkName (enum, as_ref, from_epoch, fork_version, activation_epoch), ForkSchedule (2 new fields), body_fork_layout, validate_fork_id's bound, and grpc-signer's byte-match — five sites in three crates, none of which the compiler links together.
findings.recommendation: Make ForkName the single source of truth: add `impl FromStr for ForkName` (replacing the string match in body_fork_layout), `ForkName::try_from(u32)` / `fn id(self) -> u32` (replacing validate_fork_id and the grpc-signer byte match, which should go ForkSchedule-version -> ForkName -> id), and `fn body_layout(self) -> Option<BodyForkLayout>`. Then adding a fork touches only fork.rs and the exhaustive matches the compiler flags.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: Hand-written TreeHash boilerplate repeated across 10 container types
findings.detail: Ten types (Attestation, AggregateAndProof, ElectraAttestation, ElectraAggregateAndProof, SingleAttestation, SyncCommitteeContribution, SyncAggregatorSelectionData, ContributionAndProof, BeaconBlock, BlindedBeaconBlock) each hand-implement TreeHash with the identical scaffold: tree_hash_type() -> Container, tree_hash_packed_encoding() -> unreachable!, tree_hash_packing_factor() -> 1, plus a MerkleHasher::with_leaves(N) body writing each field leaf with .expect("valid leaf"). Six of them also duplicate the try_tree_hash_root/panicking-tree_hash_root pairing with near-identical doc comments. That is roughly 250 lines where the only real content is the ordered leaf list — the same merkleization-sensitivity that block_body solved with derive.
findings.recommendation: Add one declarative macro, e.g. `impl_container_tree_hash!(ElectraAttestation, 4, [ |s| bitlist_tree_hash_root(&s.aggregation_bits, ELECTRA_AGG_BITS_LIMIT)?, |s| Ok(s.data.tree_hash_root()), |s| Ok(vec_u8_tree_hash_root(&s.signature)), |s| Ok(vec_u8_tree_hash_root(&s.committee_bits)) ]);` that emits both try_tree_hash_root and the TreeHash impl (panicking wrapper included). The leaf order stays explicit and reviewable in one place per type, and the scaffold can no longer drift.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: eth-types insecure module is dead code superseded by a diverged crypto implementation
findings.detail: eth-types/src/insecure.rs (98 lines: InsecureGate/Decision/evaluate/from_env) states in its own module doc that it has 'zero callers outside its own tests', and rg confirms: every production use of InsecureGate (bin/rvc, bin/rvc-signer, grpc-signer, remote_signer) resolves to the separate, richer implementation in crates/crypto/src/insecure.rs (closure-predicate design, env var + predicate conjunction, InsecureMode Refuse/Warn). The only outside reference to the eth-types version is a code comment in bin/rvc-signer/src/service.rs:452. The two APIs have diverged (Decision enum vs Result-based check; different env-var semantics), so the eth-types copy is now a trap for a future caller picking the wrong gate. It also contradicts ARCHITECTURE.md's contract that eth-types is 'pure data types... no business logic'.
findings.recommendation: Delete crates/eth-types/src/insecure.rs, its lib.rs export, and crates/eth-types/tests/insecure_gate.rs; fix the stale comment in bin/rvc-signer/src/service.rs to reference crypto's InsecureGate. If ADR-003 requires a shared primitive, move crypto's version down instead — but keep exactly one.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: ssz_helpers fork_id dispatch is a no-op and silently wrong for Electra attestations
findings.detail: The module doc promises helpers that 'dispatch by fork_id', but no function dispatches: all four encoders take `_fork_id` and ignore it, and the decoders only range-check it (validate_fork_id: `fork_id > 6`). decode_attestation_ssz accepts fork_id 5/6 (Electra/Fulu) yet always decodes the pre-Electra 3-field layout — ElectraAttestation (which exists in aggregation.rs) has no SSZ codec at all, so the rvc-signer aggregate path (service.rs:750) would misparse an Electra-shaped aggregate rather than reject it. On top of that, the encoders/decoders hand-roll offset arithmetic (magic constants 84, 128, 56) for containers whose sibling structs already get correct codecs from ssz_derive or impl_ssz_container!, duplicating layout knowledge in a third style.
findings.recommendation: Decide what fork_id means and enforce it: either implement real dispatch (fork_id >= 5 decodes ElectraAttestation, returning an enum or dedicated error) or delete the parameter from encode/decode signatures and validate fork at the proto boundary. Simultaneously replace the manual offset math with ssz_derive-generated codecs on the wire structs (Attestation and SyncCommitteeContribution are plain containers), keeping only the thin fork-validation wrapper.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: ~300 lines of test fixtures and KAT constants exported from the production API surface
findings.detail: external_vector_electra_body, external_vector_deneb_body, their blinded variants, four block-level builders in block.rs:354-400, six EXTERNAL_*_ROOT_HEX constants, and helper constructors (external_vector_eth1_data, external_vector_execution_payload, ...) are compiled into the production library and re-exported from lib.rs. rg shows every external consumer (crypto, beacon, block-service, bin/rvc-signer, grpc-signer — 12 files) uses them exclusively inside #[cfg(test)] modules or tests/ directories. These fixtures are pure test oracles living in the crate's public namespace, inflating the API surface a production caller must reason about and shipping fixture-construction code in release binaries.
findings.recommendation: Gate them behind a cargo feature (e.g. `test-fixtures`) in a dedicated `pub mod fixtures`, and have consuming crates declare `rvc-eth-types = { features = ["test-fixtures"] }` in dev-dependencies. Alternatively move them to a small rvc-eth-test-vectors dev-only crate.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: extract_blob_kzg_commitments hand-parses body offsets and reports malformed input as an empty list
findings.detail: block.rs:86-137 re-implements Deneb/Electra body layout knowledge by hand (DENEB_BODY_FIXED_LEN=392, KZG_COMMIT_OFFSET_POS=388, next-offset bounding for Electra) even though SEC-6 added full typed decoders (decode_beacon_block_body_deneb/electra) that already understand the same layout — the fixed-length constants are now maintained independently in block.rs and in block_body.rs tests (392/396). The function's error contract also conflates states: every failure mode (truncated body, bad offset, misalignment, over-limit count) returns vec![], indistinguishable from a legitimately empty commitment list, so BlockContents::kzg_commitment_root silently produces the empty-list fingerprint for a corrupt body. Callers on the proposal path already pay for a full typed decode in try_tree_hash_root, so the manual parser saves nothing there.
findings.recommendation: Reimplement extract_blob_kzg_commitments on top of the typed decoders (decode body for the given BodyForkLayout, return body.blob_kzg_commitments), change the signature to Result<Vec<[u8; 48]>, BodySszError> so malformed bodies are distinguishable from empty lists, and let the blob-count/root accessors propagate or explicitly log the error. Delete the duplicated offset constants from block.rs.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: Two hex-parsing stacks (hex_fixed vs canonical) with different policies, plus three pubkey representations
findings.detail: hex_fixed's bytes_hex_mod! macro and canonical::pubkey_hex both implement prefix-strip + hex-decode + length-check, with different policies (hex_fixed requires 0x and doesn't reject 0x0x; canonical accepts bare hex, rejects double prefix, and scrubs raw characters from error messages) — serde_signature.rs is a third copy of the same decode-and-length-check. canonical/mod.rs says later issues 'will migrate existing ad-hoc parsing onto these seams', but adoption stalled at two external call sites (rvc/liveness_loop.rs, slashing/db.rs). Meanwhile pubkeys have three in-crate representations: validated [u8; 48] via hex_fixed (ProposerDuty), the PubkeyHex newtype (canonical), and a completely unvalidated `pub pubkey: String` on SyncCommitteeDuty (sync_committee.rs:22).
findings.recommendation: Make canonical the single decode engine: rewrite hex_fixed's deserialize and serde_signature's deserialize to call canonical's strip_prefix/decode_hex (keeping the stricter 0x-required policy where API compatibility demands it), and convert SyncCommitteeDuty.pubkey to [u8; 48] with the bytes_48_hex serde used by ProposerDuty. Then finish or explicitly close the L-2/GVR-1 migration note in canonical/mod.rs.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: ForkSchedule's 13 parallel fields drive three hand-maintained per-fork matches, with a trace call in a pure function
findings.detail: ForkSchedule stores epoch+version as 13 flat fields, and ForkName then re-enumerates every fork three times: the descending if-else chain in from_epoch (fork.rs:47-61), the fork_version match (70-80), and the activation_epoch match (82-92) — previous_fork derives from these. Each new fork adds two struct fields and three match arms that must stay mutually consistent by hand. from_epoch also embeds tracing::trace! (fork.rs:66) in an otherwise pure lookup called on hot duty paths, which is why the crate carries a tracing dependency and a tracing-test dev-dependency.
findings.recommendation: Add `fn entries(&self) -> [(ForkName, Epoch, Version); 7]` (or an internal const-ordered slice) on ForkSchedule and implement from_epoch/fork_version/activation_epoch/previous_fork as iterations over it, so a new fork is one enum variant plus one table row. Move the trace event to the callers that select forks for signing, and drop tracing from eth-types if the insecure module (its only other user) is also removed.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: Constant-echo tests add maintenance noise without catching regressions
findings.detail: domains.rs devotes 12 tests to re-asserting each DOMAIN_* constant against the same literal written five lines above (test_domain_randao: assert_eq!(DOMAIN_RANDAO, [0x02,0,0,0])), and lib.rs does the same for SLOTS_PER_EPOCH, SECONDS_PER_SLOT, and CONSENSUS_SPEC_VERSION (test_consensus_spec_version_value asserts the exact string). These tautologies fail only if someone edits both sites, so they document nothing the constant's own definition doesn't, while doubling the diff for any legitimate constant change. The genuinely useful invariants (test_all_domains_are_unique, size check) are buried among them.
findings.recommendation: Delete the per-constant literal-echo tests, keeping test_all_domains_are_unique and the SSZ length tests. If pinning against the spec is the intent, one table-driven test comparing all domains to a single spec-cited array serves that purpose with one edit point.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: Signature = Vec<u8> alias leaves the 96-byte invariant to serde while block_body uses [u8; 96]
findings.detail: The crate-root `pub type Signature = Vec<u8>` is used by every wire type (SignedBeaconBlock, Attestation, SyncCommitteeMessage, ...), with the 96-byte invariant enforced only on the JSON deserialize path (serde_signature.rs:23) — a Signature constructed in code or decoded via ssz_helpers (which does `bytes[offset3..].to_vec()`) can be any length and flows unchecked into tree_hash leaves via vec_u8_tree_hash_root, silently producing a different root for a wrong-length signature. The typed body containers meanwhile use [u8; 96] (block_body.rs SignedBeaconBlockHeader etc.), so the two universes disagree on the representation as well as the SSZ stack.
findings.recommendation: Introduce `pub struct Signature([u8; 96])` (serde via the existing bytes_96_hex, TreeHash as the fixed vector) and migrate the wire types to it incrementally, starting with the signing-path types (SignedBeaconBlock, AggregateAndProof) where a wrong-length signature is most damaging. This also collapses serde_signature.rs into hex_fixed and removes the length checks scattered across consumer crates.
findings.scope: crates/eth-types — consensus types, SSZ codecs, hash_tree_root

findings.title: SyncService is a production-dead duplicate of orchestrator sync-committee logic
findings.detail: sync_service::SyncService (produce_sync_messages lib.rs:115-189, produce_contributions lib.rs:192-304) has zero production callers: rg shows the orchestrator imports only `is_sync_committee_aggregator` (sync_committee.rs:12) and SyncServiceError (orchestrator/error.rs:10). crates/rvc/src/orchestrator/sync_committee.rs (1,080 lines) reimplements the identical flow — zip duties/pubkeys, sign message, BTreeSet subnet dedup with the same `pos / (512/4)` expression, selection proof, aggregator check, fetch contribution, sign ContributionAndProof, submit — adding timeouts and the D-3 doppelganger gate. Safety fixes now exist in two places: the H-6 'signing failure must not abort the loop' isolation is implemented and tested in both copies, and sync-service's own KAT test (lib.rs:605-610) explicitly documents 'the byte-identical orchestrator closure at crates/rvc/src/orchestrator/sync_committee.rs:170'.
findings.recommendation: Pick one owner. Either (a) delete SyncService/SyncSigner/SyncBeaconClient and shrink sync-service to the pure functions actually used (is_sync_committee_aggregator, subnet mapping, error type), or (b) parameterize SyncService with the timeout/gating hooks the orchestrator needs and make SyncCommitteeService delegate to it. Option (a) is the cheaper immediate win; either way the ~600 lines of tests covering the dead copy stop giving false confidence.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: Doppelganger crate maintains two parallel detection implementations with duplicated restart-skip logic and clock
findings.detail: The crate ships the legacy backward-looking DoppelgangerService (String pubkeys, GVR-blind LegacySlashingHistoryReader) and the newer ForwardWindowMachine (pubkey-hex keys, GVR-aware slashing::SlashingDbReader). Both are wired in production: startup.rs:139-193 uses the legacy service, liveness_loop.rs uses the machine — even though config/builder.rs:264 labels the legacy path 'tests / non-production'. The restart-aware safe-skip guard (current_epoch > monitoring_epochs && current_epoch - epoch <= monitoring_epochs) is duplicated at service.rs:133-135 and forward_window.rs:131-132; forward_window.rs:93 admits it is 'mirroring DoppelgangerService::check_validators (service.rs:129-131)', and the M-7 pre-genesis fix had to be applied in both. Additionally DoppelgangerService embeds its own copy of the monotonic clock (fields service.rs:31-38, formula service.rs:96-101) that duplicates MonotonicEpochClock (epoch_clock.rs:23-77) line for line — epoch_clock.rs:47 even says its constructor 'mirrors DoppelgangerService::with_start_time'.
findings.recommendation: Make DoppelgangerService hold a MonotonicEpochClock instead of its own start_instant/start_unix_time fields (delete current_epoch/with_start_time duplicates). Extract the restart-skip predicate into one shared function used by both implementations. Then either retire DoppelgangerService in favor of ForwardWindowMachine for the startup path too, or document the split and unify the two slashing-reader traits behind one GVR-aware interface.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: timing::AttestationTimer and run_slot_loop are dead production code with dead metrics and constants
findings.detail: rg across crates/ and bin/ finds no use of AttestationTimer, run_slot_loop, wait_for_slot_start, or wait_for_attestation_time outside crates/timing itself — the rvc coordinator drives its own slot loop directly from SlotClock + due_ms (coordinator.rs:23). timer.rs (334 lines) self-registers three prometheus metrics (rvc_slot_timing_current_slot, rvc_slot_timing_drift_seconds, rvc_slot_timing_attestation_delay_seconds, timer.rs:16-51) that can never update in production, which is actively misleading for operators building dashboards. TimingError::SlotNotStarted (error.rs:11) has zero constructors anywhere; TimingError::Cancelled is only reachable from the dead timer. The BPS constants SYNC_MESSAGE_DUE_BPS, CONTRIBUTION_DUE_BPS, ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS_GLOAS, AGGREGATE_DUE_BPS_GLOAS (lib.rs:32-58) also have no consumers outside the crate.
findings.recommendation: Delete timer.rs, its metrics, TimingError::SlotNotStarted/Cancelled, and the unused BPS constants (or move the Gloas constants next to a TODO in the coordinator if a fork migration genuinely plans to use them). If the timer abstraction is intended to replace the coordinator's hand-rolled loop, wire it in instead — but do not keep both.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: block-service/src/service.rs is 3,567 lines — 85% one inline test module with three redundant mock beacon clients
findings.detail: Production code ends at line 565; lines 568-3567 are a single #[cfg(test)] mod with 90 tests. It contains a full 11-method ValidatorSigner mock (lines 606-776, mostly stub methods for duties block-service never signs) and three separate BeaconBlockClient mocks (MockBeaconClient:778, CapturingBeacon:1403, BoostCapturingBeacon:2097) that differ only in what they capture. Navigating or reviewing the production logic requires scrolling past ~3,000 lines of fixtures; fixture drift between the three beacon mocks is already visible.
findings.recommendation: Split the test module into files (src/service/tests/{mocks.rs, propose.rs, ssz.rs, boost.rs} or a sibling tests/ dir with a shared mod common). Merge the three beacon mocks into one configurable capturing mock. Consider a shared stub ValidatorSigner in the signer crate behind a test-utils feature (crypto already uses this pattern) so builder and block-service stop re-stubbing 11 methods each.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: DutyTracker duplicates its parse-and-cache loop four times and clear_cache misses the sync-committee cache
findings.detail: The 25-line attester duty parse loop (parse slot/committee_index/validator_index Strings, warn-and-skip on failure, insert into EpochDutyCache) is byte-identical in fetch_duties_for_epoch (tracker.rs:114-140) and check_and_refetch_if_root_changed (tracker.rs:205-230); the proposer variant is likewise duplicated (tracker.rs:326-335 vs 389-398). Any change to duty parsing must be made in four places. Separately, clear_cache (tracker.rs:299-303) clears the attester and proposer caches then logs 'Cleared all duty caches' — but never touches sync_committee_cache, so a caller relying on a full reset (e.g. after chain reorg or key change) keeps stale sync duties for up to a 256-epoch period.
findings.recommendation: Extract `EpochDutyCache::from_response(&AttesterDutiesResponse)` and `ProposerEpochDutyCache::from_response(...)` constructors and call them from both fetch and refetch paths. Add sync_committee_cache.clear() to clear_cache (or rename it clear_epoch_caches and document the exclusion). Longer term, a small generic epoch-keyed cache struct would collapse the three RwLock<HashMap<..>> + accessor triplets.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: Inconsistent signer/beacon seam design across the four duty crates
findings.detail: Each duty crate answers the 'how do I depend on signer and beacon' question differently: block-service takes generic S: ValidatorSigner (11-method fat trait) plus a narrow local 4-method BeaconBlockClient adapted via rvc/src/beacon_adapter.rs; builder takes Arc<dyn ValidatorSigner> plus the full 25-method Arc<dyn bn_manager::BeaconNodeClient>; sync-service invents its own 3-method SyncSigner/SyncBeaconClient with Vec<u8> pubkey aliases (lib.rs:20-21) and Send+Sync bounds while the others are ?Send; the orchestrator's own duty services bypass traits entirely and hold concrete Arc<SignerService>. The cost is concrete: builder's tests must stub all 25 BeaconNodeClient methods (service.rs:339-476) and all 11 signer methods (service.rs:497-603) to test two functions.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on the block-service pattern: each duty crate defines a minimal client/signer trait covering only what it calls, and rvc provides newtype adapters (beacon_adapter.rs already establishes the orphan-rule-compliant pattern). For builder this means a 2-method BuilderBeaconClient (register_validators, prepare_beacon_proposer) and a 1-method BuilderRegistrationSigner, deleting ~250 lines of mock stubs.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: SlotClock implementations duplicate ~90 lines of slot math per impl; slot/epoch helpers re-derived in sibling crates
findings.detail: SystemSlotClock (clock.rs:57-139) and MockSlotClock (clock.rs:176-249) implement the identical SlotClock methods — slot_start_time, slot_end_time, attestation_time, time_until_slot, time_until_attestation, slot_to_epoch, epoch_start_slot — differing only in the time source (SystemTime::now vs AtomicU64); the mock's time_until_attestation even carries a comment saying it 'mirrors the basis-points millisecond arithmetic used in SystemSlotClock'. Beyond timing, the same slot/epoch arithmetic is re-derived ad hoc: DutyTracker::slot_to_epoch/is_epoch_boundary_slot/sync_committee_period (tracker.rs:462-476), doppelganger's MonotonicEpochClock (epoch_clock.rs:57-72), and inline `slot / SLOTS_PER_EPOCH` in block-service (service.rs:127) and sync-service.
findings.recommendation: Refactor SlotClock so all derived methods are default trait methods computed from three required primitives (genesis_time, slot_duration, current_time_secs); SystemSlotClock and MockSlotClock then shrink to their time source only. Gate MockSlotClock behind a test-utils feature. Have MonotonicEpochClock implement the same primitive so doppelganger stops owning parallel epoch math.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: sync-committee constants and subnet mapping duplicated between sync-service and orchestrator
findings.detail: SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE=512 and SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT=4 are defined independently in sync-service (lib.rs:23-25, plus TARGET_AGGREGATORS_PER_SYNC_SUBCOMMITTEE) and in the orchestrator (sync_committee.rs:20-23), and the subnet-mapping expression `pos / (SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE / SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT)` is duplicated at sync-service lib.rs:211 and orchestrator sync_committee.rs:170. The KAT test in sync-service (lib.rs:605-642) exists specifically because the two copies can drift — it pins the mapping 'against the byte-identical orchestrator closure'. eth-types already hosts SLOTS_PER_EPOCH/SECONDS_PER_SLOT and is depended on by both crates.
findings.recommendation: Move the three sync-committee constants and a `subcommittee_index(pos) -> u64` helper (and is_sync_committee_aggregator, which depends only on them plus sha2) into eth-types or a small shared module, then delete both local copies. The KAT test collapses to one canonical location.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: Builder tests use unsafe pointer downcast to reach a mock through Arc<dyn Trait>
findings.detail: test_register_validators_no_builder_enabled recovers the MockBn from the service via `let bn = service.bn.as_ref() as *const dyn BeaconNodeClient as *const MockBn; let calls = unsafe { &*bn }.register_calls.lock();` (service.rs:669-671). This is undefined behavior waiting to happen if the field ever stops holding a MockBn, and it is unnecessary — every other test in the same file keeps an `Arc<MockBn>` clone before constructing the service (e.g. service.rs:693-705) and asserts through that.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the test to hold `let bn = Arc::new(MockBn::new())` and pass `bn.clone()` into BuilderService::new, matching the surrounding tests, and delete the unsafe block. Consider adding `unsafe_code = "forbid"` (or deny) at the workspace lint level given no production crate in this scope needs unsafe.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: propose_block_with_mode is a public validation-bypassing entry point with no production callers
findings.detail: BlockService::propose_block_with_mode (service.rs:106-113) calls propose_block_impl with `validator: None`, skipping the H-4 proposer_index/parent_root/slot validation that propose_block enforces. rg shows no callers outside block-service's own test module (the boost-factor tests at service.rs:2150-2345 use it). The crate simultaneously maintains a CI symbol-grep guard (tests/symbol_grep.rs) whose sole purpose is to prevent an unvalidated propose entry point from being reintroduced — yet this public method is exactly that, one adapter call away from misuse.
findings.recommendation: Demote propose_block_with_mode to pub(crate) or #[cfg(test)], or change its signature to require a BlockResponseValidator. If tests only need to control BlockSelectionMode, add a test-only constructor knob instead of a second public propose path, and extend the symbol-grep guard to cover it.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: sync-service API uses Vec<u8> type aliases and parallel duty/pubkey arrays
findings.detail: sync-service defines `type Signature = Vec<u8>; type PublicKey = Vec<u8>` (lib.rs:20-21) while sibling crates use crypto::PublicKey, and both public methods take parallel slices `duties: &[SyncCommitteeDuty]` + `pubkeys: &[PublicKey]` guarded by runtime length checks that produce InvalidInput errors (lib.rs:122-126 and 199-203). The pairing invariant is a caller burden the type system could enforce; SyncCommitteeDuty additionally carries its own String pubkey, giving three representations of the same identity in one call.
findings.recommendation: If SyncService survives the dedup decision (see finding 1), change the API to take `&[(SyncCommitteeDuty, crypto::PublicKey)]` (or a small DutyWithKey struct), delete the aliases and the two length-check branches, and drop the corresponding mismatched-length tests. If SyncService is deleted, this resolves itself.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: DutyTracker unit tests are wiremock HTTP integration tests coupled to beacon URL layout
findings.detail: Every test in tracker.rs (36 of them) spins up a wiremock MockServer and a real beacon::BeaconClient (setup_mock_beacon, tracker.rs:500-507), then asserts cache behavior through JSON responses matched on paths like /eth/v1/validator/duties/attester/10. The unit under test is pure cache logic behind Arc<dyn BeaconNodeClient>; the HTTP layer adds startup cost per test and couples duty-tracker's test suite to the beacon crate's endpoint scheme (a URL change in beacon breaks duty-tracker tests). beacon and wiremock exist only as dev-dependencies for this.
findings.recommendation: Test DutyTracker against an in-memory BeaconNodeClient mock returning typed AttesterDutiesResponse/ProposerDutiesResponse values (only 3 of the 25 trait methods need real implementations; the rest can be a shared stub — see finding on seam design). Keep one or two wiremock round-trip tests, or move them to tests/ as explicit integration coverage of the beacon+tracker pair.
findings.scope: Per-duty service crates: block-service, sync-service, doppelganger, builder, duty-tracker, timing

findings.title: BeaconNodeClient is a 51-method god-trait with 18 implementations, 16 of them hand-rolled mocks
findings.detail: The trait has 51 async fns covering state/config, duties, block production, attestations, sync committees, liveness, and submission. rg finds 18 `impl BeaconNodeClient for` sites; only 2 are production (BnManager, BeaconClient in crates/bn-manager/src/manager.rs:801,1239). The other 16 are per-test-module mocks (MockBeacon x5, MockBn, ToctouBeacon, TrackingBeacon, SyncGuardBeacon, ErrorBeacon, FailoverLivenessClient, ...), each stubbing all 51 methods to exercise 1-3 of them. Every method added to the trait touches ~16 files. Meanwhile block-service, sync-service, and propagator already define correctly-narrow client traits (BeaconBlockClient, SyncBeaconClient, AttestationSubmitter), so the codebase has the segregation pattern but does not apply it to the orchestrator/duty paths.
findings.recommendation: Two complementary moves: (1) split BeaconNodeClient into role traits along the existing comment sections (DutiesProvider, BlockProducer, AttestationApi, SyncCommitteeApi, LivenessApi, NodeStatusApi) with a blanket `impl<T: all-of-them> BeaconNodeClient for T` for compatibility, so tests implement only the role they exercise; (2) until/alongside that, add one canonical configurable mock (erroring-by-default, override per method) in a shared test-support crate or behind a `test-utils` feature on bn-manager, and delete the 16 copies.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: crypto is a god-crate: workspace logging registry lives inside the BLS crate, creating spurious layering edges
findings.detail: crates/crypto (11.3k LOC) contains BLS ops, EIP-2333/2335, the Web3Signer HTTP client (remote_signer.rs, 1551 LOC), AND the workspace's canonical structured-logging registry (crypto::logging — 638 LOC: RedactedUrl, `fields`, `conformance` consumed by the Gate-5 CI test). Consequences: beacon (the low-level HTTP client) imports the whole crypto stack solely for `crypto::logging::RedactedUrl` (client.rs:7); architecture-tests depends on crypto just to read the registry; bn-manager, keymanager-api and rvc/config reach into crypto::logging similarly. ARCHITECTURE.md's layer diagram shows no beacon->crypto edge — the real graph has one, purely because of logging. This also inflates rebuild fan-out: touching crypto rebuilds ~everything.
findings.recommendation: Extract crypto::logging into a new leaf crate (e.g. crates/observability or fold into an rvc-logging-core), pinned in architecture-tests' ZERO_OUT_EDGE_IF_PRESENT like telemetry already is. Then drop the crypto dependency from beacon and architecture-tests. Separately consider moving remote_signer.rs (Web3Signer HTTP client) out of crypto into its own crate parallel to grpc-signer, leaving crypto as pure key/BLS material.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: Web3Signer wire protocol duplicated between client (crypto) and server (rvc-signer) with only a comment keeping them in sync
findings.detail: remote_signer.rs defines the Serialize side of the Web3Signer body (WireForkInfo, BeaconBlockEnvelope, RandaoRevealPayload, AggregationSlotPayload, ...) with the literal comment "Shape mirrors `bin/rvc-signer/src/http_api/request.rs` (read-only reference)"; request.rs (387 LOC) defines the Deserialize side independently. There is no shared type and no round-trip test binding them, so a field rename or serde attribute change on either side silently breaks the rvc <-> rvc-signer HTTP path at runtime. The recent commit history ("fix(crypto): send Web3Signer-compliant client request bodies") shows this contract has already drifted once.
findings.recommendation: Extract the wire structs into one shared module (a small `web3signer-wire` crate, or the observability-free part of eth-types) deriving both Serialize and Deserialize, used by both crates. Add a serde round-trip conformance test in that crate so the wire contract is enforced by the type system rather than by a comment.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: Consensus-critical network preset constants duplicated in two incompatible formats
findings.detail: genesis_validators_root, genesis_fork_version, capella_fork_version, and genesis_time are defined twice: rvc-keygen holds them as [u8; N] byte arrays for mainnet/hoodi/holesky/sepolia; crates/rvc/src/config/network.rs holds them as &'static hex strings for mainnet/hoodi only (different network sets, different representations, no shared source). A wrong-GVR or wrong-fork-version drift between the two produces invalid signatures/deposits — the exact bug class the repo already patched once (commit 0fa0a42 "sign BLS-to-execution with genesis fork version"). eth-types is the natural home (it already owns ForkSchedule, domains, and has zero internal deps).
findings.recommendation: Add a `networks` module to crates/eth-types with one canonical NetworkPreset table (typed [u8;4]/[u8;32] constants plus hex accessors) and make both bin/rvc-keygen/src/network.rs and crates/rvc/src/config/network.rs thin re-exports. Add a cross-check test asserting the hex-string and byte forms agree.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: Three divergent HTTP retry implementations; the remote-signing path has none
findings.detail: beacon has a mature retry stack (execute_with_retry, execute_with_retry_raw, Retry-After parsing, exponential backoff, 4xx-no-retry policy — several hundred lines with dedicated tests). crates/rvc/src/monitoring.rs reimplements a simpler push_with_retry with its own 4xx/5xx policy and its own tests. crypto's RemoteSigner (Web3Signer client) and grpc-signer build bare clients with a timeout and no retry policy at all — so the beacon-node path is resilient but the signing path (arguably more critical per-slot) fails on a single transient error. Four reqwest::Client::builder() construction sites also each hand-configure timeouts.
findings.recommendation: Extract a small shared http-retry helper (policy enum: retry-5xx/timeout, honor Retry-After, exp backoff with cap) either as a new leaf crate or as a public module of beacon consumed by rvc/monitoring. Then make an explicit decision for RemoteSigner/GrpcRemoteSigner: adopt the shared policy with a tight per-slot deadline, and document it where the client is constructed.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md dependency graph has drifted from the real Cargo graph; architecture-tests does not check it
findings.detail: ARCHITECTURE.md says 23 crates; the workspace has 26 (architecture-tests and signer-registry are absent from the doc). The mermaid graph omits real production edges: signer->doppelganger (which architecture_no_cycles.rs enforces as REQUIRED_EDGE — the doc contradicts the CI gate), doppelganger->slashing+crypto (doc says DOPP->ETH only), block-service->builder and block-service->beacon, beacon->crypto+telemetry, bn-manager->crypto, keymanager-api->metrics, sync-service shown depending only on ETH (true) but propagator/duty-tracker edges to metrics are shown while others are not. The architecture test suite validates acyclicity, 2 forbidden edges, 1 required edge, and 3 zero-out-edge sinks — it never validates the documented graph, so the doc will keep rotting.
findings.recommendation: Either regenerate the mermaid graph from `cargo metadata` (a small generator script checked into architecture-tests, with a test asserting doc == generated), or trim ARCHITECTURE.md to the layer diagram plus the policy tables that CI actually enforces. Also update the crate count and add the two meta-crates.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: Workspace dependency hygiene: unused deps, a dead feature flag consumed by four crates, and out-of-workspace version pins
findings.detail: Statically verified unused [dependencies]: crypto's ssz_derive and tree_hash_derive (zero references in src), metrics' serde_json, grpc-signer's thiserror (it reuses crypto::SigningError exclusively). crypto declares `test-utils = []` and four crates (rvc, signer, doppelganger, block-service) request `crypto = { features = ["test-utils"] }` in dev-deps, but no code in crypto is gated on it — a dead flag that misleads readers (secret-provider's test-utils, by contrast, is real).
