Version pins bypassing [workspace.dependencies]: bn-manager's `futures = "0.3"` (production), rcgen = "0.13" duplicated in grpc-signer and rvc-signer dev-deps, hyper/http-body-util pinned in three crates, bin/rvc dev-deps re-pin toml = "0.8" and libc = "0.2" even though both exist as workspace deps. Feature naming is split: crypto/secret-provider use `test-utils`, signer uses `test-helpers`.
findings.recommendation: Remove the four unused deps; either populate crypto's test-utils with the shared keystore/signer helpers (see test-support finding) or delete the flag and its four downstream references; promote futures, rcgen, hyper, http-body-util to [workspace.dependencies]; switch bin/rvc dev-deps to `toml.workspace = true` / `libc.workspace = true`; standardize on one feature name (`test-utils`). The rustls/tokio-rustls per-crate pins in bin/rvc-signer are deliberate and well-documented — leave them.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: bin/rvc-signer is a 15.6k-LOC application crate hiding six library subsystems behind a binary
findings.detail: bin/rvc-signer has 15.6k LOC of src (largest unit after crates/rvc) plus 3.7k of integration tests, structured as a bin+lib hybrid. It contains subsystems that are libraries in all but location: http_api (Web3Signer-compatible HTTP server incl. its own TLS accept loop), dvt (Shamir shares, Lagrange, peer client), tls, audit (X.509 CN allow-list), backend (Basic/Dvt signers), slashing config, metrics. It carries 11 thiserror enums — more than any library crate. Because it all lives under bin/, none of it is reachable by the architecture-tests layer policy for libraries, per-crate analyzers will treat it as one blob, and grpc-signer's integration tests must re-create server fixtures (rcgen PKI, mTLS servers) instead of reusing server test helpers.
findings.recommendation: Promote the reusable subsystems to crates/ (e.g. rvc-signer-core with backend+dvt+tls+audit+http_api), keep bin/rvc-signer as CLI parsing + config merge + startup wiring only. This puts the code under the same layering gates as everything else and lets grpc-signer's tests spin up a real in-process server from the library.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: Crate topology: propagator is a 695-LOC pass-through that should merge; block-service depends on all of builder for one type
findings.detail: propagator (695 LOC, 2 files) defines AttestationSubmitter with a blanket impl over every BeaconNodeClient plus logging/metrics around submit calls — it is a thin decoration of bn-manager's submit path, yet costs a crate boundary, its own error enum, and a Cargo.toml. block-service imports `builder::CircuitBreakerState` (service.rs:3) as its only use of builder, pulling in the whole MEV-registration crate (and its bn-manager subtree) for one struct and creating a domain->domain edge the ARCHITECTURE.md layer model says should not exist. signer-registry (196 LOC) is fine as-is: it is deliberately dev-only per ADR-010 and pinned in the CI gate — do not merge it. sync-service (1k LOC, deps only eth-types) is small but correctly isolated.
findings.recommendation: Fold propagator into bn-manager as a `submit` module (keeping the AttestationSubmitter trait public for DI) or into the rvc orchestrator; move CircuitBreakerState into a small shared location (eth-types has no deps and is the wrong home semantically — a `service-util` module in signer or a tiny shared crate is better, or have block-service define its own state and builder convert) so block-service->builder disappears; then add the restored "no domain->domain edges" rule to architecture-tests' FORBIDDEN table.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: No shared test-support crate: keystore, mock-signer, and TLS-PKI fixtures are copy-pasted across the workspace
findings.detail: `create_test_keystore` is implemented four times inside bin/rvc-signer alone (split_key.rs, integration_polish.rs, backend/basic.rs, reload.rs) with slightly different signatures; rcgen-based mTLS PKI + start_mtls_server fixtures are duplicated between crates/grpc-signer/tests/integration.rs and bin/rvc-signer/tests/dvt_sni_pinning_l1.rs; MockSigner exists 4x and MockBeacon-family mocks 16x (see god-trait finding). The workspace already has per-crate `test-utils`/`test-helpers` features but no central home, and crypto's test-utils feature is empty — the natural place for keystore fixtures already exists and gates nothing.
findings.recommendation: Create the shared fixtures where consumers already look for them: put `create_test_keystore`/key-generation helpers behind crypto's currently-empty `test-utils` feature; put the rcgen PKI + mTLS server harness in a dev-only `rvc-test-support` crate (publish = false, pinned dev-only in architecture-tests like signer-registry). Then delete the copies.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: Two parallel shutdown idioms: tokio::watch in the core loop vs CancellationToken in services
findings.detail: Graceful shutdown is signalled two ways: tokio::watch channels in the orchestrator coordinator, bn-manager (sse.rs, sync_status.rs, manager.rs), timing, and slashing_monitor; tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken in secret-provider/refresh, keymanager-api/handlers, rvc/{monitoring,liveness_loop,config_url}, and both binaries. bin/rvc/src/main.rs uses both and must bridge them. Every new service has to pick one and wire an adapter at the boundary; cancellation semantics (level vs edge, child tokens) differ subtly between the two.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on CancellationToken (already the majority in newer code, supports hierarchies via child_token) as the workspace idiom; migrate the watch-based loops opportunistically (bn-manager and coordinator first, since bin/rvc already holds the bridge), and record the choice in ARCHITECTURE.md's design-patterns list.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: Metrics are registered through four independent patterns/registries with heavy expect boilerplate
findings.detail: crates/metrics owns the default-registry lazy_static pattern (36 registration sites; 48 of the workspace's 210 production expects are its create+register double-expect pairs — the single biggest unwrap/expect hotspot). But secret-provider ships its own src/metrics.rs with its own lazy_static block, timing registers metrics inline in timer.rs, and bin/rvc-signer/src/metrics.rs builds a separate Registry for :9101. That leaks prometheus + lazy_static as direct deps into timing and secret-provider and means naming conventions (rvc_* prefixes) are enforced only by convention. Remaining unwrap/expect hotspots for reference: eth-types block.rs (21) and aggregation.rs (21) are justified fixed-size-slice expects; rvc-signer metrics.rs (20) is the same registration pattern.
findings.recommendation: Add a `register_metric!` (or small generic fn) in crates/metrics that does create+register+expect once, and re-export prometheus/lazy_static (or std::sync::LazyLock on rust 1.92) from crates/metrics so satellite crates stop declaring them. Move secret-provider's and timing's definitions into their crates but built via the shared helper against the shared registry; keep rvc-signer's separate Registry (deliberate isolation) but on the same macro.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: Small consistency drifts: anyhow inside a library crate, scattered 0x-prefix hex handling
findings.detail: Error-strategy discipline is otherwise excellent (thiserror in all 22 libraries, anyhow only in binaries), but crates/telemetry uses anyhow in its public init API (init.rs, config.rs, file_appender.rs) — the one library violating the project's own CLAUDE.md rule, and it forces bin consumers to string-match errors instead of matching variants. Separately, `trim_start_matches("0x")`/`strip_prefix("0x")` is hand-rolled in 15+ production files across 8 crates even though crypto/src/hex.rs exists as the canonical hex module (and a canonical parse layer exists in eth-types/src/canonical/).
findings.recommendation: Give telemetry a small thiserror TelemetryError (InvalidSampleRate, ExporterInit, AppenderInit cover current uses) and drop anyhow from its Cargo.toml. Route 0x-normalization through one helper (crypto::hex or eth-types::canonical) and add it to the field-conformance-style lint list so new hand-rolled copies get flagged in review.
findings.scope: rvc workspace cross-cutting analysis (26 crates, ~135k LOC)

findings.title: Hand-rolled SSZ/tree-hash and opaque Vec<u8> BeaconBlockBody instead of typed containers
findings.detail: AUDIT-2026-05-30 identifies hand-rolled Merkleization (manual MerkleHasher field writes, vec_u8_tree_hash_root, BeaconBlockBody = Vec<u8>) as the root cause of its four worst findings (C-1, C-2, C-3, H-1, H-2); AUDIT-2026-07-18 #7 confirms C-2 still unfixed; plan/security-2026-07-18 SEC-6a-d is the tracked remediation cluster (11-16 pts). Recent commit 2493c3a ('Deneb and blinded body hash_tree_root coverage') suggests this is in flight — verify completion state before planning.
findings.recommendation: Complete the SEC-6 direction: replace hand-rolled hash_tree_root for all consensus containers with typed structs using tree_hash_derive whose field order mirrors the spec; delete tree_hash_utils.rs manual merkleization; add known-answer vectors from a reference client for every container root.
findings.scope: Prior review/audit corpus for rvc workspace (REVIEW.md, CODE_REVIEW_REPORT.md, AUDIT-2026-05-30.md, AUDIT-2026-07-18-known-issues.md, test-audit-report.md, .claude/rvc-review-*.md, docs/issues/, plan/security-2026-07-18/)

findings.title: Safety mechanisms built but not wired into production paths (systemic pattern)
findings.detail: AUDIT-2026-05-30 theme 4 and AUDIT-2026-07-18 'recurring pattern 1' both flag that correct mechanisms exist in-tree but are never connected: ForwardWindowMachine + SigningGate (constructed nowhere outside tests; production uses the inert backward one-shot doppelganger — C-4), startup-gate exit codes never propagated to process exit (M-11), is_usable*() helpers dead while optimistic-sync gating is bypassed (H-6), brute-force decryption tracker never wired (L-1), gRPC remote signer fully implemented but dead-wired. SEC-2a-c tracks the doppelganger wiring.
findings.recommendation: Audit every guard/gate end-to-end for wiring, not existence; wire ForwardWindowMachine/SigningGate into bin/rvc per SEC-2; delete or wire the remaining dead mechanisms; add a convention that safety components ship with an integration test proving the production binary invokes them.
findings.scope: Prior review/audit corpus for rvc workspace (REVIEW.md, CODE_REVIEW_REPORT.md, AUDIT-2026-05-30.md, AUDIT-2026-07-18-known-issues.md, test-audit-report.md, .claude/rvc-review-*.md, docs/issues/, plan/security-2026-07-18/)

findings.title: Keymanager API bookkeeping (tracked_keys) diverges from the real signing registry
findings.detail: AUDIT-2026-07-18 #1 and its 'recurring pattern 2': KeystoreManagerAdapter.tracked_keys is populated only by API import, so boot-loaded validators are invisible to list/delete — DELETE returns not_found while the key keeps signing, and delete returns an empty slashing interchange for a key with history. The fix is fundamentally a refactor: make the Keymanager operate on the single source of truth (ValidatorStore/pubkey_map) instead of a parallel partial view. Tracked as SEC-1a/1b.
findings.recommendation: Eliminate the parallel tracked_keys registry; route list/delete/has_key through ValidatorStore, and add a persistent deletion denylist consulted by all key sources (secret-provider re-load included).

findings.title: Widespread .unwrap()/.expect() in production hot paths
findings.detail: REVIEW.md (2026-04-01) rates this the top remaining High: ~1,082 .expect() and ~2,523 .unwrap() in non-test code across 85+ files, concentrated in crypto, eth-types, orchestrator, beacon. A concrete instance (H-5, keystore IV panic) was empirically reproduced as a startup/import DoS in AUDIT-2026-05-30 and AUDIT-2026-07-18 #6 (tracked as SEC-5).
findings.recommendation: Incremental campaign: convert panic points in the per-slot hot path first (coordinator, beacon client, signing paths) to Result propagation; add clippy lints (unwrap_used/expect_used deny in those crates) to prevent regression.

findings.title: Tests encode wrong spec assumptions; self-consistency tests cannot catch spec divergence
findings.detail: AUDIT-2026-05-30 theme 2: three separate bugs (C-1, C-2, H-9) each had a green test asserting the bug — e.g. test_electra_attestation_tree_hash_spec_field_order enforced the wrong field order, and compute_block_root == tree_hash_root is tautological self-consistency. The 03-08 review's 'fix' for Electra field order was inverted to match a mis-stated spec because no external oracle existed.
findings.recommendation: Adopt known-answer-vector testing for every signing root and container root, sourced from reference clients / official consensus-spec tests; forbid relative/self-consistency assertions as the sole coverage for spec-defined values.

findings.detail: test-audit-report HIGH #2-6: MockBeaconClient ignores the slot param in produce_block_v3; publish_block discards the SignedBeaconBlock (only consensus_version captured); MockSigner ignores fork_schedule/genesis_validators_root; sync-committee mocks discard all submitted messages and ignore signer inputs — so wrong-argument and wrong-domain bugs pass all tests. findings.recommendation: Refactor mocks to capture full call arguments and submitted payloads (CapturingSubmitter pattern already used in coordinator tests), then assert on content, not counts.

findings.title: No integration test proving slashing protection blocks a conflicting signature through the full pipeline
findings.detail: test-audit-report CRITICAL #1: every coordinator test uses a fresh in-memory SlashingDb and one slot; no test processes two slots with conflicting data, so a refactor that bypasses the AttestationService→SignerService slashing wiring goes undetected. Related HIGH #7: the concurrent same-validator signer test uses identical data so it passes even with the per-validator mutex removed; HIGH #8: no fail-closed test for DB errors. Tracked as docs/issues phase-1 items 1.3/2.5/2.6.
findings.recommendation: Add a pipeline-level double-vote rejection test (process_slot twice with conflicting AttestationData), fix the concurrent test to use conflicting data, and add a fail-closed DatabaseError propagation test.

findings.title: Fail-open error handling at security-critical edges
findings.detail: AUDIT-2026-05-30 theme 5: the stated fail-closed signing principle is not uniformly applied — delete_keystores deleted keys on export error (H-7, since fixed), refresh-discovered keys go live with no doppelganger gate (M-8, open), doppelganger marks missing liveness indices safe (L-6), and the slashing DB silently creates a fresh empty DB on missing/0-byte file (AUDIT-2026-07-18 #4, SEC-3). The pattern, not the individual bugs, is the refactoring target.
findings.recommendation: Establish a shared fail-closed convention (e.g. typed Result flows with explicit allow-lists for degradation) and sweep the key-lifecycle and DB-open edges against it; SEC-3 and SEC-2 cover the two open concrete instances.

findings.title: Inconsistent signer/slashing API surfaces invite misuse
findings.detail: CODE_REVIEW_REPORT: sign_attestation takes Fork while all other sign methods take ForkSchedule (L-11); is_safe_to_sign/is_safe_to_propose diverge from their atomic check-and-record variants (M-26); insert_attestation/insert_block are public but bypass slashing checks (L-16). rvc-review-slashing.md additionally flags db.rs:1253-1450 prune/watermark functions as dead code with no production callers (which is also why AUDIT M-1's <= bug is currently dormant).
findings.recommendation: Unify the signing trait on ForkSchedule; make the non-atomic check variants and raw insert_* private or remove them; delete or productionize the dead prune/watermark block (fixing M-1's <= before any caller lands).

findings.title: Validator-store locking is ad hoc: inconsistent lock ordering and non-atomic multi-lock writes
findings.detail: AUDIT-2026-05-30 M-10: effective_config and save_config acquire the two RwLocks in opposite order — potential deadlock of the proposal/attestation hot path; CODE_REVIEW_REPORT M-13: reload_config performs non-atomic multi-lock writes; L-22: RwLock::read().unwrap() panics on poison (rest of the workspace moved to parking_lot per REVIEW.md).
findings.recommendation: Refactor ValidatorStore to a single lock over one state struct (or parking_lot with a documented lock-order invariant); make reload_config swap state atomically.

findings.title: Beacon client request hygiene: no URL encoding, ad hoc retry/backoff policy
findings.detail: CODE_REVIEW_REPORT H-3: query parameters (graffiti, pubkeys) interpolated without URL encoding; H-4: publish_block_ssz uniquely lacked retry while all other endpoints retry (asymmetric policy); M-31/AUDIT M-3: 429 handling inconsistent (non-retryable in one review, double-sleeping in the next); L-29: backoff has no jitter; M-32: GET query can exceed URL length for large validator sets. The scatter of per-endpoint policies is the structural issue.
findings.recommendation: Centralize request building (reqwest Url::query_pairs_mut everywhere) and a single retry/backoff policy (with jitter and Retry-After handling) applied uniformly across all beacon endpoints; switch large validator queries to POST.
